Right there, having placed down the fuel bundle for the Agnīṣomīya [animal sacrifice], the sprinkling [takes place].
The strewing [is done] with the grass broom; the Prastara is not taken in the afternoon.
When half the fast-milk has been given, having entered, the laying on of the Praṇayanīya fire takes place.

8.6.s: ājyādhiśrayaṇasruksaṃmārjanodvāsanāvekṣaṇāni kṛtvā śālādvāryam apareṇāste yajamāna upasthe somaṃ kṛtvā //
8.6.d: आज्याधिश्रयणस्रुक्संमार्जनोद्वासनावेक्षणानि कृत्वा शालाद्वार्यम् अपरेणास्ते यजमान उपस्थे सोमं कृत्वा ॥
8.6.m:
Having performed the placing of the clarified butter on the fire, the wiping of the ladles, the removal from the fire, and the inspection, the sacrificer sits to the west of the Śālādvārya fire, holding the soma in his lap.

[The Adhvaryu] scatters around to the west of the Śālādvārya fire the dust from the footprint of the soma-purchasing cow.
According to some, [he scatters it] in four parts: on the supporting embers of the Āhavanīya, on those of the Āgnīdhrīya, and on the anointings of the two axles.
Having purified the clarified butter and the sprinkling waters at the Antaḥpātya place, the taking of the clarified butter for the animal [sacrifice takes place].
And those observing the vow touch the sacrificer from behind.

8.7.s: pradīptam idhmam \\ tvam̐ soma \\ iti pracaraṇyābhijuhoti //
8.7.d: प्रदीप्तम् इध्मम् \\ त्वम्̐ सोम \\ इति प्रचरण्याभिजुहोति ॥
8.7.m: Over the blazing fuel bundle he makes an offering with the Pracaranī ladle with the mantra: 'Thou, O Soma...'
[He makes] the second [offering] with: 'Enjoying, swift in water...'
He causes [the Hotṛ] to recite for Agni being carried forward;
or with the words: 'for Soma being led forward.'

8.7.s: āhavanīyaṃ gachanty ādāya grāvadroṇakalaśasomapātrāṇīdhmaṃ catuṣṭayaṃ ca saṃnaddhaṃ vapāśrapaṇyau raśane śakalavṛṣaṇam araṇī ca //
8.7.d: आहवनीयं गछन्त्य् आदाय ग्रावद्रोणकलशसोमपात्राणीध्मं चतुष्टयं च संनद्धं वपाश्रपण्यौ रशने शकलवृषणम् अरणी च ॥
8.7.m: They proceed to the Āhavanīya fire, carrying the pressing stones, the Droṇakalaśa trough, the soma vessels, the fuel bundle, the four tied-up items, the two roasting spits for the omentum, the two cords, the piece [of wood] with its base, and the two churning sticks.
Having carried [the fire] north of the Sadas, he deposits the fire in the Āgnīdhra [shed];
and also the pressing stones, the Droṇakalaśa trough, and the soma vessels.
He offers into this [fire with the mantra]: 'May this [Agni] for us...'
Walking around to the north, they deposit everything else to the north of the Āhavanīya fire, except the clarified butter and the soma.
There is no intervention of the hearths for the Adhvaryu.
He performs the rites beginning with the sprinkling of the fuel bundle.
On the northern half of the mound [there is] a single-layer strewing [of grass];

8.7.s: āhavanīyekṣaṇāt kṛtvā \\ uru viṣṇo \\ iti juhoti //
8.7.d: आहवनीयेक्षणात् कृत्वा \\ उरु विष्णो \\ इति जुहोति ॥
8.7.m: Having performed [the rites] up to the inspection of the Āhavanīya fire, he offers with: 'Widely, O Viṣṇu...'

8.7.s: purastād vā samidhāv ādhāya \\ iti śruteḥ //
8.7.d: पुरस्ताद् वा समिधाव् आधाय \\ इति श्रुतेः ॥
8.7.m: Or, in front, having laid two kindling sticks on the fire, according to the scripture.

8.7.s: āsādyājyāni dakṣiṇe 'nasi kṛṣṇājinam āstīrya tasmint somaṃ nidadhāti deva savitar iti //
8.7.d: आसाद्याज्यानि दक्षिणे ऽनसि कृष्णाजिनम् आस्तीर्य तस्मिन्त् सोमं निदधाति देव सवितर् इति ॥
8.7.m: Having set down the portions of clarified butter, having spread the black antelope skin in the southern cart, he deposits the soma upon it with the mantra: 'O divine Savitṛ...'
Having released [it] with: 'This is thee...', he stands revering [it].

8.7.s: svāhā nir iti niṣkramya \\ agne vratapās \\ ity āhavanīye samidham ādhāya madantīr upaspṛśyāṅgulīr visṛjate //
8.7.d: स्वाहा निर् इति निष्क्रम्य \\ अग्ने व्रतपास् \\ इत्य् आहवनीये समिधम् आधाय मदन्तीर् उपस्पृश्याङ्गुलीर् विसृजते ॥
8.7.m: Having stepped out with 'Svāhā to Nir[ṛti]', having placed a kindling stick on the Āhavanīya fire with: 'O Agni, guardian of vows...', and having touched the boiling water, he releases his fingers.
And the wife [does the same] at the Gārhapatya fire, silently, having touched the boiling water.
Having made the boiling water at the Cātvāla pit.
From this point onward, they use his name and provide him with food.
The animal sacrificial cake has that same deity.

8.8.m: He brings the Iḍā of the animal to the south of the Havirdhāna cart-shed;
[and] the tail portion to the south of the Mārjālīya [hearth];
or having brought it back, so that there is no separation between the soma and the Āhavanīya fire.
If there are eleven sacrificial posts, the intervals are of the measure of a chariot axle;
or having divided the eastern half equally;
The offering for the post, the taking of the wooden spade, and the strewing of barley are performed only once.
The rest is performed separately, because of its direct application [to each post].
Having traced around the middle [post-hole], [he traces] the northern one;
the others alternately. He performs [the rites] up to the offering into the hole.
Having performed [the rites] beginning with anointing up to looking at the top-ring for each one,

8.8.s: śvo vā dakṣiṇottarāṇām avagūhanāntam ālambhanāsambhavāt parivīya madhyamam avagūhanāntam //
8.8.d: श्वो वा दक्षिणोत्तराणाम् अवगूहनान्तम् आलम्भनासम्भवात् परिवीय मध्यमम् अवगूहनान्तम् ॥
8.8.m: Or on the following day, for those to the south and north, up to tucking in [the ropes], because the immolation cannot take place [yet]; having encircled the middle post, [the procedure] ends with tucking in.
And on the central post he winds the cord up to the top ring and lets it rest [overnight].
He performs [the rites] beginning with the anointing.
He erects [them] according to the hole dug [for each].
In a sacrifice with intensive pressing (tīvrasutyā), the central post is [tallest], and the line runs eastward.
The enlargement of the altar corresponds to the [number of] sacrificial posts.

8.8.s: varṣiṣṭhād dakṣiṇaṃ vitaṣṭaṃ dvādaśaṃ nidadhāti \\ eṣa te \\ iti //
8.8.d: वर्षिष्ठाद् दक्षिणं वितष्टं द्वादशं निदधाति \\ एष ते \\ इति ॥
8.8.m: To the south of the tallest [post], he deposits a twelfth, roughly hewn [post], with [the mantra]: "This is for thee..."
He performs [the rites] from sprinkling up to tucking in, omitting what has no practical purpose.

He seizes the animals for the pressing (savanīya) according as [the posts] have been erected, having brought [them] up with a single blade of grass: [the victims] belonging to Agni, Sarasvatī, Soma, Pūṣan, Bṛhaspati, the Viśve Devas, Indra and the Maruts, Indrāgnī, Savitṛ, and Varuṇa.

8.8.s: ekayūpe paśvekādaśinyām āgneyaṃ niyujya tasmiṃstasminn itarān udīcaḥ //
8.8.d: एकयूपे पश्वेकादशिन्याम् आग्नेयं नियुज्य तस्मिंस्तस्मिन्न् इतरान् उदीचः ॥
8.8.m: When there is a single post in the set of eleven animals, having bound the [victim] belonging to Agni, [he binds] the others one after another toward the north.

8.8.d: आग्नेयः प्रथमो गछत्य् अन्वारब्धो ऽनुपूर्वा इतरे ॥
8.8.m: The [victim] for Agni goes first, held from behind; the others follow in order.

8.8.s: dakṣiṇaṃ ca nighnanty enam uttaramuttaram itarān //
8.8.d: दक्षिणं च निघ्नन्त्य् एनम् उत्तरमुत्तरम् इतरान् ॥
8.8.m: And they kill this [first victim] to the south, and the other [victims] successively toward the north.

Common are: the call for prompting, the subsidiary offering to each animal, the mantra "Silence him!", the walking along behind, the sprinkling water, the firebrand, the knife, the slaughtering place, the screen, the cutting off [of organs], the summons for the drops, the instruction to the slaughterer, the dialogue, the [offerings of the] Vanaspati, the Sviṣṭakṛt, and the Iḍā.
The trickling to the quarters is done after pouring [the broth] together.
A spit and two omentum-cooking spits [are used for each victim].
And on account of what is seen in the Sautrāmaṇī.
In the Sautrāmaṇī [different pots are used] because of the difference in cooking [times].
The Manotā hymn and the fat-oblation are separate, because of the difference in time.

8.8.s: yūpaikādaśinyāṃ vaśāvapāmārjanāntaṃ kṛtvā śālādvārye patnīyūpochrayaṇaṃ nābhimātrasya //
8.8.d: यूपैकादशिन्यां वशावपामार्जनान्तं कृत्वा शालाद्वार्ये पत्नीयूपोछ्रयणं नाभिमात्रस्य ॥
8.8.m: In the set of eleven posts, having performed [the rites] up to the cleansing after the omentum of the barren cow, the erection of the wife's post, measuring navel-high, takes place at the Śālādvārya fire.
Having performed the strewing, placing of the vessels, sprinkling, pouring out of ghee, and placing [it] over the fire, he performs [the rites] beginning with the wooden sword.

8.9.m: They release it after carrying fire around it.
Because of the Vedic text: "He completes [the rite] with ghee."
And because the carrying of fire around the animal has taken place.
Or it ends with that, because of the name of the rite.
And because an offering to Tvaṣṭṛ and Vanaspati is seen among the fore-offerings.
At the end of the cleansing after the omentum of the animal for Agni and Soma, the drawing of the Vasatīvarī waters from flowing [waters takes place] before sunset.
If the sun has set, from a reservoir, if he has sacrificed before.
If he has not sacrificed before, from [the water] of another person settled nearby who has sacrificed before.

8.9.s: ubhayābhāva ulkuṣīm̐ hiraṇyaṃ voparyupari dhārayan haviṣmatīr iti //
8.9.d: उभयाभाव उल्कुषीम्̐ हिरण्यं वोपर्युपरि धारयन् हविष्मतीर् इति ॥
8.9.m: In the absence of both, holding a burning firebrand or gold above [the vessel, he draws] with [the mantra]: "Possessing oblation..."

8.9.s: agner vas \\ iti nidadhāti śālādvāryam apareṇa //
8.9.d: अग्नेर् वस् \\ इति निदधाति शालाद्वार्यम् अपरेण ॥
8.9.m: He sets [the vessel] down to the west of the Śālādvārya fire with [the mantra]: "Of Agni you are..."
And he prompts for the Subrahmaṇyā litany including fathers and sons.
Even when the sun has set, though [the Agnihotra] has not been offered.

8.9.s: dakṣiṇāgnihomāntam agnīṣomīyam astamite sam̐sthāpya vyutkrāmata \\ ity āha triḥ //
8.9.d: दक्षिणाग्निहोमान्तम् अग्नीषोमीयम् अस्तमिते सम्̐स्थाप्य व्युत्क्रामत \\ इत्य् आह त्रिः ॥
8.9.m: Having concluded the [animal sacrifice] to Agni and Soma at sunset ending with the offering in the Dakṣiṇāgni, he says three times: "Step apart!"
The wife sits to the west of the Śālādvārya fire.

8.9.s: uttaravedim apareṇa yajamāna upasthe somaṃ kṛtvā //
8.9.d: उत्तरवेदिम् अपरेण यजमान उपस्थे सोमं कृत्वा ॥
8.9.m: The sacrificer, having placed the soma on his lap, sits to the west of the high altar.
He carries the Vasatīvarī waters around to the west of the Śālādvārya fire.

8.9.s: dakṣiṇena nirhṛtya dakṣiṇasyām uttaravediśroṇau nidadhāti \\ indrāgnyor iti //
8.9.d: दक्षिणेन निर्हृत्य दक्षिणस्याम् उत्तरवेदिश्रोणौ निदधाति \\ इन्द्राग्न्योर् इति ॥
8.9.m: Having carried [them] out by the south, he sets [them] down on the southern hip of the high altar with [the mantra]: "Of Indra and Agni..."
Having taken [the vessel] up, he sets [it] down in its place.
The wife touches the pitcher.
Having gone around by the north, [he places it] on the northern [hip] as before.
In the Āgnīdhra fire-shed with [the mantra]: "Of the Viśve Devas..."

8.9.s: dīkṣitaś ca tatra tām̐ rātrim̐ somam̐ rakṣati //
8.9.d: दीक्षितश् च तत्र ताम्̐ रात्रिम्̐ सोमम्̐ रक्षति ॥
8.9.m: And the consecrated [sacrificer] guards the soma there during that night.
And he prompts for the Subrahmaṇyā litany.
Resting at home, rubbing down, adorning, and brushing the teeth are permitted for the unconsecrated Adhvaryu priest.

9.1.m: In the latter part of the night, they awaken the officiating priests.

9.1.s: apa upaspṛśya śālādvārye paristaraṇapātrasam̐sādanaprokṣaṇājyanirvapaṇādhiśrayaṇasruksaṃmārjanodvāsanāvekṣaṇāni kṛtvāgnīdhra utpūya paśvājyagrahaṇam //
9.1.d: अप उपस्पृश्य शालाद्वार्ये परिस्तरणपात्रसम्̐सादनप्रोक्षणाज्यनिर्वपणाधिश्रयणस्रुक्संमार्जनोद्वासनावेक्षणानि कृत्वाग्नीध्र उत्पूय पश्वाज्यग्रहणम् ॥
9.1.m: Having touched water, having performed at the Śālādvārya fire the strewing, placing of the vessels, sprinkling, pouring out of ghee, placing [it] over the fire, wiping the ladles, taking [the ghee] off [the fire], and inspecting [it], and having purified [it] in the Āgnīdhra shed, the scooping of animal-ghee takes place.

9.1.s: ājyāny ādāya somaṃ cāryavac cāhavanīya idhmaprokṣaṇādi karoti //
9.1.d: आज्यान्य् आदाय सोमं चार्यवच् चाहवनीय इध्मप्रोक्षणादि करोति ॥
9.1.m: Having taken the ghees and the soma in the manner prescribed for an Ārya, he performs at the Āhavanīya fire [the rites] beginning with the sprinkling of the fuel bundle.
The strewing [of the sacrificial grass is performed] like that for the animal sacrifice to Agni and Soma.

9.1.s: ājyāsādanāt kṛtveṣāntarenārdhasomam adriṣu saṃmukheṣu nidadhāti hṛde tvā \\ iti //
9.1.d: आज्यासादनात् कृत्वेषान्तरेनार्धसोमम् अद्रिषु संमुखेषु निदधाति हृदे त्वा \\ इति ॥
9.1.m: Having performed up to the depositing of the ghee, he places half the soma between the two shafts upon the pressing-stones facing one another, with [the mantra]: "For the heart thee..."
Having released it with [the mantra]: "All [the hymns]... thee", he stands worshipping.
With this, the bringing forward of the Soma-portion takes place during the pressing.
There is no taking out [of the Soma], because it remains outside of it.
And there is no taking down of what has been pressed, because that has already been done.

9.1.s: prāg vācaṃ pravaditoḥ prātaranuvākopākaraṇam \\ devebhyaḥ prātaryāvabhyo 'nubrūhi \\ iti samidham ādadhat //
9.1.d: प्राग् वाचं प्रवदितोः प्रातरनुवाकोपाकरणम् \\ देवेभ्यः प्रातर्यावभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहि \\ इति समिधम् आदधत् ॥
9.1.m: Before speech starts to be spoken, the commencement of the morning recitation takes place, while placing a piece of firewood [on the fire with the formula]: 'Recite for the gods who come in the morning!'
And he summons the Subrahmaṇyā recitation.
The Adhvaryu priest should attend the morning recitation while staying awake.
The Agnīdh priest pours out [the sacrificial substance for a cake] on eleven potsherds for Indra.
Clotted curd for Mitra and Varuṇa.
Or for Indra accompanied by the two bay steeds, Pūṣan, Sarasvatī, and Mitra and Varuṇa, [he pours out] the parched grains and the rest in corresponding order.

9.2.m: On the north-eastern half of the mound [are placed the cups] for the Upāṃśu and Antaryāma.
To the west of that, facing west, [are placed] the cups for two deities.
The cup for Indra and Vāyu has a girdle-like moulding.
The cup for Mitra and Varuṇa has the shape of a goat's foot.
On the south-eastern half [are placed the cups] of the Śukra and Manthin.
The Āgrayaṇa vessel is in the middle.
To the south is the Ukthya vessel with its cup.
Likewise the Āditya vessel is to the north.

9.2.s: ṛtupātre pūrve srukpuṣkarākṛtī ubhayatomukhe kārṣmaryamaye āśvatthe vā //
9.2.d: ऋतुपात्रे पूर्वे स्रुक्पुष्कराकृती उभयतोमुखे कार्ष्मर्यमये आश्वत्थे वा ॥
9.2.m: The two Ṛtu cups, placed to the east, shaped like the bowl of a ladle, two-mouthed, are made of kārṣmarya wood or of aśvattha wood.
The others are upright, a span in size, and narrow in the middle.
West of the Āgrayaṇa vessel, [he places] the Pariplavā spoon, shaped like the bowl of a ladle.

9.2.s: adho'dho 'kṣaṃ pratyañcaṃ droṇakalaśam atyuhyoparyupary akṣaṃ pavitram asmin karoti śuklaṃ jīvorṇānām //
9.2.d: अधोऽधो ऽक्षं प्रत्यञ्चं द्रोणकलशम् अत्युह्योपर्युपर्य् अक्षं पवित्रम् अस्मिन् करोति शुक्लं जीवोर्णानाम् ॥
9.2.m: Having pushed the Droṇakalaśa trough westward, below the axle, he places a white filter of wool from a living animal over the axle upon it.
[A filter] fringed on both ends [is placed] in the Pariplavā spoon.
East of the northern prop, he places the Dhruvā vessel directly upon the ground.
East of the axle, above, the Pūtabhṛt vessel.

9.2.s: prāg akṣād daśa camasānt savṛntān adhaḥ //
9.2.d: प्राग् अक्षाद् दश चमसान्त् सवृन्तान् अधः ॥
9.2.m: East of the axle, below, [he places] ten cups with handles.

9.2.s: pratyag ekadhanān ayugmān udaharaṇāṃs triprabhṛtyā pañcadaśabhyaḥ //
9.2.d: प्रत्यग् एकधनान् अयुग्मान् उदहरणांस् त्रिप्रभृत्या पञ्चदशभ्यः ॥
9.2.m: To the west, the Ekadhana water-pitchers, an odd number, from three up to fifteen.
While [the verse] 'Dawn has shone forth with her bright cattle...' is being recited,

9.3.s: caturgṛhītaṃ pracaraṇyā juhoti śṛṇotv agnir iti //
9.3.d: चतुर्गृहीतं प्रचरण्या जुहोति शृणोत्व् अग्निर् इति ॥
9.3.m: He offers four ladlings with the Pracaraṇī spoon with the formula: 'May Agni hear...'

9.3.s: aparaṃ gṛhītvodaṅ gachann āha \\ apa iṣya hotar iti //
9.3.d: अपरं गृहीत्वोदङ् गछन्न् आह \\ अप इष्य होतर् इति ॥
9.3.m: Having taken another [four ladlings], while walking northwards, he says: 'Hotṛ priest, impel the waters!'
And he prompts: 'O Camasādhvaryu of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest, come!

9.3.s: agnīc cātvāle vasatīvarībhiḥ pratyupatiṣṭhāsai hotṛcamasena ca \\ iti //
9.3.d: अग्नीच् चात्वाले वसतीवरीभिः प्रत्युपतिष्ठासै होतृचमसेन च \\ इति ॥
9.3.m: O Agnīdh priest, attend at the Cātvāla pit with the Vasatīvarī waters and with the cup of the Hotṛ priest!'

9.3.s: apo gatvā devīr āpas \\ ity apsu juhoti //
9.3.d: अपो गत्वा देवीर् आपस् \\ इत्य् अप्सु जुहोति ॥
9.3.m: Having gone to the water, he makes an offering into the water with the formula: 'O divine waters...'
With the formula: 'You are the furrow...', he pushes away the ghee with the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest.
With the formula: 'Thee of the ocean...', he takes [water] with that [cup].
And they draw the Ekadhana pitchers.
And the wives [draw water for] washing the feet, two [pitchers] each.

9.3.s: pratyetya cātvālasyopari maitrāvaruṇacamasaṃ vasatīvarīś ca sam̐sparśayati sam āpas \\ iti //
9.3.d: प्रत्येत्य चात्वालस्योपरि मैत्रावरुणचमसं वसतीवरीश् च सम्̐स्पर्शयति सम् आपस् \\ इति ॥
9.3.m: Having returned, above the Cātvāla pit, he touches the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest and the Vasatīvarī waters together with the formula: 'May the waters unite...'
Some pour [a little water] mutually into each other.
First into the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest.

9.3.s:
hotṛcamase vasatīvarīḥ kṛtvā yajamānāya prayachati nigrābhyāḥ //
hotrā pṛṣṭaḥ pratyāha \\ uteva naṃnamur iti //
9.3.d:
होतृचमसे वसतीवरीः कृत्वा यजमानाय प्रयछति निग्राभ्याः ॥
होत्रा पृष्टः प्रत्याह \\ उतेव नंनमुर् इति ॥
9.3.m: Having put the Vasatīvarī waters into the cup of the Hotṛ priest, he gives them to the sacrificer for the Nigrābhyā waters. / When asked by the Hotṛ priest, he replies: 'And they have bowed down...'

9.3.s: pracaraṇīsam̐sravam agniṣṭome juhoty abhāve caturgṛhītam \\ yam agne \\ iti //
9.3.d: प्रचरणीसम्̐स्रवम् अग्निष्टोमे जुहोत्य् अभावे चतुर्गृहीतम् \\ यम् अग्ने \\ इति ॥
9.3.m: At an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice, he offers the residue in the Pracaraṇī spoon, or in the absence of residue, four ladlings, with the formula: 'O Agni, whom...'
At an Ukthya sacrifice, he touches the first enclosing stick.
Or at a Ṣoḍaśin sacrifice, there is the touching of the fronton.

9.3.s: atītya dakṣiṇena hotāraṃ maitrāvaruṇacamasam ādhavanīye 'vanayati vasatīvaritṛtīyaṃ ca \\ agniḥ prātaḥsavane pātv asmān \ vaiśvānaro mahīnāṃ viśvaśambhūḥ \ sa naḥ pāvako draviṇaṃ dadhātu \\ āyuṣmantaḥ sahabhakṣāḥ syāma \\ iti //
9.3.d: अतीत्य दक्षिणेन होतारं मैत्रावरुणचमसम् आधवनीये ऽवनयति वसतीवरितृतीयं च \\ अग्निः प्रातःसवने पात्व् अस्मान् \ वैश्वानरो महीनां विश्वशम्भूः \ स नः पावको द्रविणं दधातु \\ आयुष्मन्तः सहभक्षाः स्याम \\ इति ॥
9.3.m: Passing beyond the Hotṛ priest to the south, he pours the cup of the Maitrāvaruṇa priest and one-third of the Vasatīvarī waters into the Ādhavanīya trough with the formula: 'May Agni protect us at the morning pressing, Vaiśvānara, who brings all blessings to the great [waters]; may he, purifying, grant us wealth; may we, having long life, share in the consumption!'
After placing the remainder of both in the place of the Ekadhana [waters],

9.4.m: they sit around the pressing boards.
To the north are the Adhvaryu and the sacrificer,
Having gone around to the west, the other three [sit].

9.4.s: devasya tvā \\ ity adrim ādāya vācaṃ yachati prāg ghiṅkārāt //
9.4.d: देवस्य त्वा \\ इत्य् अद्रिम् आदाय वाचं यछति प्राग् घिङ्कारात् ॥
9.4.m: Taking the pressing stone with [the mantra], 'At the impulse of god Savitṛ...', he restrains his speech until the hiṅkāra chant.

9.4.s: nigrābhyāsu vācayaty urasy enā nigṛhya nigrābhyā stha \\ iti //
9.4.d: निग्राभ्यासु वाचयत्य् उरस्य् एना निगृह्य निग्राभ्या स्थ \\ इति ॥
9.4.m: He makes [the sacrificer] recite over the Nigrābhyā waters, holding them firmly against his chest: 'You are the Nigrābhyā waters...'

9.4.s: upām̐śusavane somaṃ mimīte \\ indrāya tvā vasumate rudravate \\ iti pañcakṛtvaḥ pratimantram //
9.4.d: उपाम्̐शुसवने सोमं मिमीते \\ इन्द्राय त्वा वसुमते रुद्रवते \\ इति पञ्चकृत्वः प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
9.4.m: He measures out the soma on the Upāṃśusavana stone with: 'For Indra accompanied by the Vasus, accompanied by the Rudras...', five times, once with each mantra.
Touching what has been measured is done with: 'What of you...'
The Pratiprasthātṛ takes six soma shoots.
He places them two by two between his fingers.
He pours the Nigrābhyā waters with: 'You are invigorating...'

9.4.s: prahariṣyan dveṣyaṃ manasā dhyāyet \\ amuṣmā ahaṃ praharāmi na tubhyam̐ soma \\ iti //
9.4.d: प्रहरिष्यन् द्वेष्यं मनसा ध्यायेत् \\ अमुष्मा अहं प्रहरामि न तुभ्यम्̐ सोम \\ इति ॥
9.4.m: About to strike, he should mentally reflect on the enemy: 'I strike him, not you, O Soma.'
Thus he presses three times, each time preceded by the pouring of the Nigrābhyā waters:
eight times, eleven times, [and] twelve times.
All [groups] consist of sets of five for one desirous of cattle;
sets of eight for one desirous of spiritual luster.

9.4.s: prativargaṃ nigrābhaṃ vācayati hotṛcamase 'lpān am̐śūn avadhāya prāg apāg iti //
9.4.d: प्रतिवर्गं निग्राभं वाचयति होतृचमसे ऽल्पान् अम्̐शून् अवधाय प्राग् अपाग् इति ॥
9.4.m: At each group, having placed a few soma shoots in the Hotṛ's cup, he makes him recite the Nigrābha [mantra]: 'Forward, backward...'

9.4.s: upām̐śu ca gṛhṇāti vācaspataye \ devo devebhyas \\ madhumatīr iti //
9.4.d: उपाम्̐शु च गृह्णाति वाचस्पतये \ देवो देवेभ्यस् \\ मधुमतीर् इति ॥
9.4.m: And he draws the Upāṃśu cup with: 'To the lord of speech...', 'A god to the gods...', 'Containing sweetness...'
The Pratiprasthātṛ holds the vessel underneath.
And he interposes two of those taken each time, because of the distinct drawings,
or [he interposes all] six, due to the significance of the scripture.

9.4.s: yat te \\ ity āttānt some nidadhāti //
9.4.d: यत् ते \\ इत्य् आत्तान्त् सोमे निदधाति ॥
9.4.m: With 'What of you...' he places the taken [shoots] into the soma.
The wiping around and depositing of the Upāṃśu and Antaryāma cups [are performed].

9.4.s: abhicarant sādayed avisṛjann amuṣya tvā prāṇam̐ sādayāmi \\ iti //
9.4.d: अभिचरन्त् सादयेद् अविसृजन्न् अमुष्य त्वा प्राणम्̐ सादयामि \\ इति ॥
9.4.m: One performing malevolent sorcery should deposit [the cup] without releasing it, with: 'I deposit the breath of so-and-so.'

9.4.s: pāṇinā cāpidadhāti \\ amuṣya tvā prāṇam apidadhāmi \\ iti //
9.4.d: पाणिना चापिदधाति \\ अमुष्य त्वा प्राणम् अपिदधामि \\ इति ॥
9.4.m: And he covers it with his hand, with: 'I cover the breath of so-and-so.'

9.4.s: svāhā \\ ity uktvā \\ urv antarikṣam iti niṣkramaṇam //
9.4.d: स्वाहा \\ इत्य् उक्त्वा \\ उर्व् अन्तरिक्षम् इति निष्क्रमणम् ॥
9.4.m: Having spoken 'Svāhā!', the going out is performed with: 'The wide atmosphere...'
Having handed the Hotṛ's cup to another, he touches him from behind.
Having offered with 'Well prepared...', he wipes the vessel.

9.4.s: prathame paridhā uttānaṃ pāṇiṃ prāg upamārṣṭi devebhyas tvā \\ iti //
9.4.d: प्रथमे परिधा उत्तानं पाणिं प्राग् उपमार्ष्टि देवेभ्यस् त्वा \\ इति ॥
9.4.m: On the first enclosing stick, he wipes off [the residue] facing east with his hand turned upward, with: 'For the gods, you...'

9.4.s: vāsaurobāhuṣu śliṣṭam am̐śum abhicaran juhuyād devām̐śo \\ iti //
9.4.d: वासौरोबाहुषु श्लिष्टम् अम्̐शुम् अभिचरन् जुहुयाद् देवाम्̐शो \\ इति ॥
9.4.m: One performing malevolent sorcery should offer a shoot sticking to his garment, chest, or arms, with: 'O divine shoot...'
Having poured a portion of the remainder into the Āgrayaṇa vessel, he casts a shoot into it for the third soma pressing.
The depositing of the vessel is done with: 'For the breath, you...'

9.4.s: upām̐śusavanaṃ pāṇinā pramṛjyodañcam \\ vyānāya tvā \\ iti sam̐spṛṣṭam //
9.4.d: उपाम्̐शुसवनं पाणिना प्रमृज्योदञ्चम् \\ व्यानाय त्वा \\ इति सम्̐स्पृष्टम् ॥
9.4.m: Having wiped the Upāṃśusavana stone with his hand toward the north, [he deposits it] touching [the vessel], with: 'For the dispersed breath, you...'

9.5.m: four [priests] press [soma], on account of the purpose of sitting around.
The pressing, ending with the swelling [of the shoots], has three rounds,
The pouring of the Nigrābhyā waters occurs at the beginning of the rounds,
or only in the first [round], because of sufficiency.
At the end of the Nigrābha, having placed the juicy shoots into the Sambharaṇī vessel and the Ādhavanīya trough, and having shaken them, he brings them back.
Or, in the earlier [action], having drawn the Upāṃśu cup, [they do not perform] the swelling and gathering, because it has already been performed.
The sitting around is merely a ritual duty.

9.5.s: abhiṣavaviparyāso vābhimṛṣṭād am̐śūn apakṛṣya nigrābhyāś cānupūrvyayogāt //
9.5.d: अभिषवविपर्यासो वाभिमृष्टाद् अम्̐शून् अपकृष्य निग्राभ्याश् चानुपूर्व्ययोगात् ॥
9.5.m: Or there is an alteration of the pressing, because the shoots are drawn away from what was touched, and the Nigrābhyā waters are applied in sequence,
and because of the possibility of measuring what was not taken,

9.5.s: prohya droṇakalaśam ṛjīṣam ukheṣv adriṣu nidadhaty udgātāraḥ //
9.5.d: प्रोह्य द्रोणकलशम् ऋजीषम् उखेष्व् अद्रिषु निदधत्य् उद्गातारः ॥
9.5.m: Having pushed forward the Droṇakalaśa trough, the Udgātṛ priests deposit the residue on the stones in the pots,
and they spread out the strainer northward.

9.5.s: ādhavanīyād unnetā nigrābhyāsv āsiñcati tāḥ pavitre yajamānas tato grahagrahaṇam ā dhruvāt //
9.5.d: आधवनीयाद् उन्नेता निग्राभ्यास्व् आसिञ्चति ताः पवित्रे यजमानस् ततो ग्रहग्रहणम् आ ध्रुवात् ॥
9.5.m: From the ādhavanīya vessel the Unnetṛ priest pours into the nigrābhyā waters; the sacrificer [pours] them onto the strainer; from that takes place the drawing of the soma cups up to the Dhruva cup.
And at the midday soma pressing, the first five.
Those that are depleted after the Sāvitra, Pātnīvata, and Hāriyojana cups [are drawn] from the Āgrayaṇa cup.
At the third soma pressing, the Vaiśvadeva cup [from the pūtabhṛt].
If [it applies to] those not specifically mentioned, because of the Vedic text prescribing drawing [from it].

9.5.s: daśāpavitreṇa parimṛjyaparimṛjya \\ eṣa te yonir iti grahasādanam //
9.5.d: दशापवित्रेण परिमृज्यपरिमृज्य \\ एष ते योनिर् इति ग्रहसादनम् ॥
9.5.m: Wiping [each] repeatedly with the fringed strainer, the setting down of the soma cup is performed with: "This is your womb..."
Vātsya says: "In all [soma cups], because the instruction is without distinction."
And because of the prohibition regarding the Sāvitra and Ṛtu cups.
Having made an offering at each vaṣaṭ-call, the bringing of the portion for consumption to the one who made the vaṣaṭ-call [takes place].
Or first to the one who made the vaṣaṭ-call, because of the authority of the Vedic text.
The Unnetṛ priest draws [the soma into the cups], on account of the designation [of his name].

9.6.m: When [the sun] has risen, the drawing of the Antaryāma cup takes place with: "Taken with a base are you..."
It is like the Upām̐śu cup, except for the unprescribed boon and the pouring out of the residue.
And on the first [cup], with the hand turned downward, toward the west.
The setting down of the vessel, which has touched the pressing stone for the Upām̐śu cup, takes place with: "For upward breath, to you..."
He draws the Aindravāyava cup with: "Come, O Vāyu..."
Having drawn it away, again [he draws] with: "O Indra and Vāyu..."
The Maitrāvaruṇa cup with: "This for both of you..."

9.6.s: payasā śrīṇāty enaṃ kuśāv antardhāya rāyā vayam iti //
9.6.d: पयसा श्रीणात्य् एनं कुशाव् अन्तर्धाय राया वयम् इति ॥
9.6.m: He mixes it with milk, placing two kuśa blades between, with: "May we with wealth..."
Thus everywhere during mixings.

9.6.s: śukraṃ bailvena vā taṃ pratnathā \\ iti //
9.6.d: शुक्रं बैल्वेन वा तं प्रत्नथा \\ इति ॥
9.6.m: The Śukra cup, or with one made of bilva wood, with: "That in the ancient way..."
The Manthin cup with: "This Vena..."

9.6.s: saktubhiḥ śrīṇāty enam \\ mano na yeṣu \\ iti //
9.6.d: सक्तुभिः श्रीणात्य् एनम् \\ मनो न येषु \\ इति ॥
9.6.m: He mixes it with barley groats with: "In whom like mind..."

9.6.s: āgrayaṇaṃ dvayor dhārayor ye devāsas \\ iti //
9.6.d: आग्रयणं द्वयोर् धारयोर् ये देवासस् \\ इति ॥
9.6.m: The Āgrayaṇa cup from two streams with: "Which gods..."

9.6.s: daśāpavitreṇāgrayaṇam upagṛhya trir hiṅkṛtya somaḥ pavate \\ iti sakṛcheṣam //
9.6.d: दशापवित्रेणाग्रयणम् उपगृह्य त्रिर् हिङ्कृत्य सोमः पवते \\ इति सकृछेषम् ॥
9.6.m: Having held the fringed strainer under the Āgrayaṇa cup and having uttered 'hiṅ' thrice, [he recites] once the remainder with: "Soma purifies itself..."
In the lowest pitch before the mention of the deity.
And the loud rites at the morning soma pressing [are performed in this pitch].
In the middle [pitch] at the midday soma pressing.
In the highest [pitch] at the third soma pressing.
The Ukthya cup with: "Taken with a base are you..."
The Dhruva cup with: "Head of heaven..."

9.6.s: ā homād asya sunvan na mūtrapurīṣe kuryāt //
9.6.d: आ होमाद् अस्य सुन्वन् न मूत्रपुरीषे कुर्यात् ॥
9.6.m: Until its offering, the presser should not discharge urine or feces.

9.6.s: ardhapūrṇaṃ droṇakalaśaṃ kṛtvā sarvam āsiñcati sunvan //
9.6.d: अर्धपूर्णं द्रोणकलशं कृत्वा सर्वम् आसिञ्चति सुन्वन् ॥
9.6.m: Having filled the droṇakalaśa half-full, the presser pours all [the remaining soma into it].
Holding onto one another, the Adhvaryu priest, Pratiprasthātṛ priest, Prastotṛ priest, Udgātṛ priest, Pratihartṛ priest, and the presser walk out.
The Adhvaryu priest first, the others according to their enumeration.
Or they may hold onto one another after having made the offering.

9.6.s: yas te \\ iti vipruṣām̐ homaṃ juhvati //
9.6.d: यस् ते \\ इति विप्रुषाम्̐ होमं जुह्वति ॥
9.6.m: They offer the oblation of drops with: "Whatever of you..."
The Adhvaryu priest takes two grass blades from the altar.
Bent forward, they proceed toward the north.

9.6.s: anyatarat tṛṇaṃ cātvāle prāsyati devānām iti //
9.6.d: अन्यतरत् तृणं चात्वाले प्रास्यति देवानाम् इति ॥
9.6.m: He throws one grass blade into the Cātvāla pit with: "Of the gods..."
The other [he places] silently in front of the Udgātṛ priests.

9.6.s: japatsu somaḥ pavate \\ iti pavamānopākaraṇaṃ prastotre tṛṇe prayachan //
9.6.d: जपत्सु सोमः पवते \\ इति पवमानोपाकरणं प्रस्तोत्रे तृणे प्रयछन् ॥
9.6.m: While they murmur "Soma purifies itself...", the initiation of the chant [is made] handing over the two grass blades to the Prastotṛ priest.

9.7.m: Facing west, the two sit down in front [of the Udgātṛs].

9.7.s: stūyamāna unnetādhavanīyaṃ pavitram antardhāya pūtabhṛty āsiñcati //
9.7.d: स्तूयमान उन्नेताधवनीयं पवित्रम् अन्तर्धाय पूतभृत्य् आसिञ्चति ॥
9.7.m: While the chant is being sung, the Unnetṛ priest, having placed the strainer over [it], pours [soma from] the ādhavanīya into the pūtabhṛt.

9.7.s: stotrānte preṣyati \\ agnīd agnīn vihara \ barhi stṛṇīhi \ puroḍāśā3m̐ alaṅkuru \ pratiprasthātaḥ paśunehi \\ iti //
9.7.d: स्तोत्रान्ते प्रेष्यति \\ अग्नीद् अग्नीन् विहर \ बर्हि स्तृणीहि \ पुरोडाशा3म्̐ अलङ्कुरु \ प्रतिप्रस्थातः पशुनेहि \\ इति ॥
9.7.m: At the end of the chant, he issues the call: "Agnīdh priest, distribute the fires; strew the sacrificial grass; adorn the sacrificial cakes; Pratiprasthātṛ priest, come with the animal!"
He scatters embers from the Āgnīdhra fire onto the hearth mounds as they were thrown up.
he strews the sacrificial grass along the spinal line.

9.7.s: āśvinaṃ gṛhṇāty anvārabdhe vā yā vām iti //
9.7.d: आश्विनं गृह्णात्य् अन्वारब्धे वा या वाम् इति ॥
9.7.m: He draws the Āśvina cup with 'yā vām…', or while [the sacrificer] holds onto him.

9.7.s: grahān avekṣayati yathāgṛhītam avakāśān vācayan prāṇāya me \\ iti //
9.7.d: ग्रहान् अवेक्षयति यथागृहीतम् अवकाशान् वाचयन् प्राणाय मे \\ इति ॥
9.7.m: He makes [the sacrificer] look at the soma cups in the order they were drawn, making him recite the avakāśa-formulas: 'For my out-breath…'.
[He looks at] the Upām̐śusavana stone second.
[He looks at] the Śukra and Manthin cups simultaneously.
And [he looks at] the Pūtabhṛt and Ādhavanīya troughs with 'For all my [limbs]…'.
He should make known, dear, and learned persons look [at them].

9.8.s: dhruvagopaṃ kṛtvā parivyayaṇādi karoti raśanām uduhya pūrvām //
9.8.d: ध्रुवगोपं कृत्वा परिव्ययणादि करोति रशनाम् उदुह्य पूर्वाम् ॥
9.8.m: Having made [someone] guard the Dhruva cup, he performs the rites beginning with the wrapping [of the sacrificial post], pushing up the earlier rope.
In the Agniṣṭoma, the animal offering connected with the soma pressing is dedicated to Agni.
In the Ukthya, there is a second [animal offering], dedicated to Indra and Agni.
In the Ṣoḍaśin, there is a third [animal offering]: a ram dedicated to Indra.
In the Atirātra, there is a fourth [animal offering], dedicated to Sarasvatī,
Having carried out [the rite] up to the mention of the Hotṛ's name, he formally chooses the other [priests] according to their characteristics, calling for each announcement again and again:
'The two Aśvins as the two Adhvaryus from the Adhvaryu's office';
'Mitra and Varuṇa as the two directors from the director's office';
The Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin priest with 'Indra as Brahman from the Brāhmaṇa's office';
The sacrificer with 'Agni indeed of the divine…'.

9.8.s: yathāpravṛtaṃ pravṛtahomau juhvati juṣṭo vāce bhūyāsam \\ juṣṭo vācaspataye \ devi vāg yat te vāco madhumattamaṃ juṣṭatamaṃ tasmin mā dhāḥ \ svāhā sarasvatyai \\ iti //
9.8.d: यथाप्रवृतं प्रवृतहोमौ जुह्वति जुष्टो वाचे भूयासम् \\ जुष्टो वाचस्पतये \ देवि वाग् यत् ते वाचो मधुमत्तमं जुष्टतमं तस्मिन् मा धाः \ स्वाहा सरस्वत्यै \\ इति ॥
9.8.m: As they are chosen, they offer the two election oblations with: 'May I be pleasing to speech, pleasing to the lord of speech! O divine speech, establish me in whatever of your speech is sweetest and most pleasing. Svāhā to Sarasvatī!'

9.8.s: vapāmārjanāntaṃ kṛtvā sayajamānā dhiṣṇyān upatiṣṭhante vibhūr asi \\ iti pratimantram //
9.8.d: वपामार्जनान्तं कृत्वा सयजमाना धिष्ण्यान् उपतिष्ठन्ते विभूर् असि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
9.8.m: Having carried out [the rite] up to the wiping after the omentum offering, [the priests] along with the sacrificer revere the dhiṣṇya hearths with 'You are widespread…', formula by formula.

9.8.s: utkarāntaṃ kṛtvā vāg asi \\ iti sado'bhimarśanam //
9.8.d: उत्करान्तं कृत्वा वाग् असि \\ इति सदोऽभिमर्शनम् ॥
9.8.m: Having carried out [the rite] up to the rubbish heap, the touching of the sadas hut is done with 'You are speech…'.
[He touches] the two door-posts with 'The two doors of truth…'.
The addressing [of the entities is done] with the subsequent [mantras]:
The sun with 'O lord of the pathways of the pathways…';
The officiating priests with 'May Mitra [look upon] me…';
The dhiṣṇya hearths with 'The Agnis together…'.

9.9.m: Or, in the subsequent two soma pressings, [the creeping] begins with the touching of the sadas hut.

9.9.s: madhye puroḍāśaḥ purastād dhānāḥ pratidiśam itarāṇi yathāsaṃkhyaṃ pradakṣiṇam //
9.9.d: मध्ये पुरोडाशः पुरस्ताद् धानाः प्रतिदिशम् इतराणि यथासंख्यं प्रदक्षिणम् ॥
9.9.m: In the middle is the cake, in front the roasted grains, and the other [substances] in each direction in order clockwise.
He calls for the recitation of the invitatory verses: 'For Indra of the morning pressing, [recite for the offerings] of the cakes.'

9.9.s: āśrāvyāha prātaḥ prātaḥsavasyendrāya puroḍāśān prasthitān preṣya \\ iti //
9.9.d: आश्राव्याह प्रातः प्रातःसवस्येन्द्राय पुरोडाशान् प्रस्थितान् प्रेष्य \\ इति ॥
9.9.m: Having called for the announcement, he says: 'For Indra of the morning pressing, urge [the Hotṛ] for the cakes that have been brought forward.'
In this way, the invitatory recitation and the directions correspond to each soma pressing.
Both are like the animal cake.
Having offered, he places the cakes on the Hotṛ's dhiṣṇya hearth,
He causes [the Hotṛ] to recite the invitatory verse: 'For Vāyu, for Indra and Vāyu…'.

9.9.s: pratiprasthātādityapātreṇa droṇakalaśāt \\ upayāmagṛhīto 'si \\ iti gṛhītvāgṛhītvā dvidevatyān anu juhoty uttarārdhe //
9.9.d: प्रतिप्रस्थातादित्यपात्रेण द्रोणकलशात् \\ उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि \\ इति गृहीत्वागृहीत्वा द्विदेवत्यान् अनु जुहोत्य् उत्तरार्धे ॥
9.9.m: The Pratiprasthātṛ priest, having drawn [soma] repeatedly from the Droṇakalaśa trough with the vessel of the Āditya cup with 'You are taken with a support…', offers on the northern half following each of the cups for pairs of deities.
And the calls for announcement, the responses, and the directions [take place], because of equality.

9.9.s: śeṣam̐śeṣam ādityasthālyām āsiñcati \\ ādityebhyas tvā \\ iti //
9.9.d: शेषम्̐शेषम् आदित्यस्थाल्याम् आसिञ्चति \\ आदित्येभ्यस् त्वा \\ इति ॥
9.9.m: He pours each remainder into the Āditya vessel with 'For the Ādityas, you…'.
Having poured them together, he covers [the vessel] with it with 'O wide-striding Viṣṇu…'.
He causes [the Hotṛ] to recite the invitatory verse for [the cups] that are being filled.
He draws [soma] into nine cups, having placed them west of the high altar.
The under-spreading and dripping [are taken] from the Śukra cup.

9.10.m: The two perform [the rites] with the Śukra and Manthin [cups].
The Adhvaryu with the Śukra, the Pratiprasthātṛ with the Manthin.
Taking two splinters of the sacrificial post, one sprinkled and one unsprinkled,
covering [the cups] with the two sprinkled ones,

9.10.s: apamārjanam aprokṣitābhyām apamṛṣṭaḥ śaṇḍas \\ ity adhvaryur apamṛṣṭo markas \\ iti pratiprasthātā //
9.10.d: अपमार्जनम् अप्रोक्षिताभ्याम् अपमृष्टः शण्डस् \\ इत्य् अध्वर्युर् अपमृष्टो मर्कस् \\ इति प्रतिप्रस्थाता ॥
9.10.m: and wiping off with the two unsprinkled ones: "Śaṇḍa is wiped away," says the Adhvaryu; "Marka is wiped away," says the Pratiprasthātṛ.
They step out according to the characteristic marks with: "May the gods thee…"

9.10.s: apareṇottaravedim aratnī saṃdhāyottaravediśroṇyor nidhatto 'visṛjantau dakṣiṇasyām adhvaryur uttarasyāṃ pratiprasthātā \\ anādhṛṣṭāsi \\ iti //
9.10.d: अपरेणोत्तरवेदिम् अरत्नी संधायोत्तरवेदिश्रोण्योर् निधत्तो ऽविसृजन्तौ दक्षिणस्याम् अध्वर्युर् उत्तरस्यां प्रतिप्रस्थाता \\ अनाधृष्टासि \\ इति ॥
9.10.m: Having joined elbows west of the high altar, without letting go, they deposit [the splinters] on the buttocks of the high altar—the Adhvaryu on the southern, the Pratiprasthātṛ on the northern—with: "Thou art unassailable."

9.10.s: suvīras \\ iti dakṣiṇaṃ yūpadeśaṃ gachaty adhvaryuḥ //
9.10.d: सुवीरस् \\ इति दक्षिणं यूपदेशं गछत्य् अध्वर्युः ॥
9.10.m: With: "Possessing good heroes…" the Adhvaryu goes to the southern side of the sacrificial post.
With: "Possessing good offspring…" the Pratiprasthātṛ [goes] to the northern [side].

9.10.s: apareṇa yūpam aratnī saṃdhattaḥ saṃjagmānas \\ iti yathāliṅgam //
9.10.d: अपरेण यूपम् अरत्नी संधत्तः संजग्मानस् \\ इति यथालिङ्गम् ॥
9.10.m: West of the sacrificial post they join elbows according to the characteristic marks with: "Coming together…"

9.10.s: aprokṣitau nirasyatas \\ nirastaḥ śaṇḍas \\ ity adhvaryur nirasto markas \\ iti pratiprasthātā //
9.10.d: अप्रोक्षितौ निरस्यतस् \\ निरस्तः शण्डस् \\ इत्य् अध्वर्युर् निरस्तो मर्कस् \\ इति प्रतिप्रस्थाता ॥
9.10.m: They throw away the two unsprinkled [splinters]: "Śaṇḍa is cast out," says the Adhvaryu; "Marka is cast out," says the Pratiprasthātṛ.

9.10.s: āhavanīye prokṣitau prāsyataḥ śukrasyādhiṣṭhānam ity adhvaryur manthinas \\ iti pratiprasthātā //
9.10.d: आहवनीये प्रोक्षितौ प्रास्यतः शुक्रस्याधिष्ठानम् इत्य् अध्वर्युर् मन्थिनस् \\ इति प्रतिप्रस्थाता ॥
9.10.m: They throw the two sprinkled ones into the Āhavanīya: "The abode of Śukra," says the Adhvaryu; "Of Manthin," says the Pratiprasthātṛ.

9.10.s: achinnasya \\ iti japitvāśrāvyāha prātaḥ prātaḥsavasya śukravato madhuścuta indrāya somān prasthitān preṣya \\ iti //
9.10.d: अछिन्नस्य \\ इति जपित्वाश्राव्याह प्रातः प्रातःसवस्य शुक्रवतो मधुश्चुत इन्द्राय सोमान् प्रस्थितान् प्रेष्य \\ इति ॥
9.10.m: Having muttered: "Of the unsevered…" and having made [the Agnīdh] respond, he says: "At the morning pressing, summon [the Hotṛ to recite] for Indra for the somas that are set out, accompanied by Śukra, dripping with sweetness!"

9.11.s: ubhayatoyūpaṃ pratyaṅmukhau juhutaḥ sā prathamā \\ ity adhvaryuḥ prathamaṃ tam anu pratiprasthātā //
9.11.d: उभयतोयूपं प्रत्यङ्मुखौ जुहुतः सा प्रथमा \\ इत्य् अध्वर्युः प्रथमं तम् अनु प्रतिप्रस्थाता ॥
9.11.m: On both sides of the sacrificial post, facing west, they offer: "This first one…"—the Adhvaryu first, the Pratiprasthātṛ following him.

9.11.s: preṣyati ca praitu hotuś camasaḥ pra brahmaṇaḥ prodgātṝṇāṃ pra yajamānasya \ pra yantu sadasyānām \\ hotrāṇāṃ camasādhvaryava upāvartadhvam \\ śukrasyābhyunnayadhvam iti //
9.11.d: प्रेष्यति च प्रैतु होतुश् चमसः प्र ब्रह्मणः प्रोद्गातॄणां प्र यजमानस्य \ प्र यन्तु सदस्यानाम् \\ होत्राणां चमसाध्वर्यव उपावर्तध्वम् \\ शुक्रस्याभ्युन्नयध्वम् इति ॥
9.11.m: And he summons: "Let the cup of the Hotṛ go forward! Let [the cup] of the Brahman go forward! Let [the cup] of the Udgātṛs go forward! Let [the cup] of the sacrificer go forward! Let [the cups] of the Sadasyas go forward! Camasādhvaryus of the Hotra-priests, turn back! Draw from the Śukra!"
Having come, the Pratiprasthātṛ pours the remainder into the Śukra cup.

9.11.s: tān āśrāvyāśrāvya preṣyati nāmagrāham \\ yajayaja \\ iti praśāstrādīn //
9.11.d: तान् आश्राव्याश्राव्य प्रेष्यति नामग्राहम् \\ यजयज \\ इति प्रशास्त्रादीन् ॥
9.11.m: Having repeatedly made [the Agnīdh] respond, he summons [them] addressing each by name: "Recite the yājyā! Recite the yājyā!" to the Praśāstṛ and the others.
"O Brahman, recite the yājyā!" to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin.

9.11.s: prathamam̐ hutvottamaṃ vā tṛmpantu \\ iti japati //
9.11.d: प्रथमम्̐ हुत्वोत्तमं वा तृम्पन्तु \\ इति जपति ॥
9.11.m: Having offered the first or the last, he mutters: "May they be satisfied…"

9.11.s: hotāraṃ pratyaṅṅ upasīdati \\ ayāḍ agnīd iti //
9.11.d: होतारं प्रत्यङ्ङ् उपसीदति \\ अयाड् अग्नीद् इति ॥
9.11.m: He sits down facing west near the Hotṛ [saying]: "The Agnīdh has sacrificed."
He consumes [the soma of] the cups for two deities.
The first [priest consumes], on account of the primary injunction;
Because of the scriptural statement: "The one who performs the offering and the pressing should consume."
Or the Hotṛ [consumes], on account of explicit statement, the wording of the mantra, and the rationale.
Not the Adhvaryu, because of the co-mention;

9.11.s: aindravāyavaṃ pratigṛhṇāti \\ aitu vasuḥ purūvasur iti //
9.11.d: ऐन्द्रवायवं प्रतिगृह्णाति \\ ऐतु वसुः पुरूवसुर् इति ॥
9.11.m: He accepts the Aindravāyava cup with: "May the wealthy, the richly-endowed come…"

9.11.s: hotṛvad bhakṣaṇam \\ vāg devī juṣāṇā somasya tṛpyatu \ saha prāṇena svāhā \\ iti //
9.11.d: होतृवद् भक्षणम् \\ वाग् देवी जुषाणा सोमस्य तृप्यतु \ सह प्राणेन स्वाहा \\ इति ॥
9.11.m: The consumption is like that of the Hotṛ: "May the divine Speech, being pleased, be satisfied with soma; svāhā together with breath!"
In this manner is the consumption of the somas everywhere;

9.11.s: bhakṣe hi mā \\ iti vā yathāliṅgam //
9.11.d: भक्षे हि मा \\ इति वा यथालिङ्गम् ॥
9.11.m: Or with: "For consumption me…" according to the characteristic mark.

9.11.s: evam itarau pratimantram aitu vasur vidadvasur \ aitu vasuḥ saṃyadvasur iti //
9.11.d: एवम् इतरौ प्रतिमन्त्रम् ऐतु वसुर् विदद्वसुर् \ ऐतु वसुः संयद्वसुर् इति ॥
9.11.m: In the same way the other two with their respective mantras: "May the wealthy, the finder of wealth come…" and "May the wealthy, the accumulator of wealth come…"
He pours each remainder into the Hotṛ's cup.
He throws a portion of the sacrificial cake into the Aindravāyava [cup];
Curds into the Maitrāvaruṇa;

9.11.s: tāni pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasyottare vartmani nidadhāti //
9.11.d: तानि प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्योत्तरे वर्त्मनि निदधाति ॥
9.11.m: The Pratiprasthātṛ deposits them on the northern track of the southern Havirdhāna [cart].

9.12.m: When [the vessel] is cleaned, they perform [the rite] with the whey, because the Sūktavāka and the Śaṃyuvāka have a different purpose;
Or as stated [before], because it is not an accidental matter.
The two consume the soma with the Hotṛ's cup.

9.12.s: hinva me gātrāṇi harivaḥ \ śivo me saptaṛṣīn upatiṣṭhasva \\ ūrdhvaṃ me nābheḥ sīda \ mā me 'vāṅ nābhim atigās \\ iti gātrāṇi sam̐spṛśante //
9.12.d: हिन्व मे गात्राणि हरिवः \ शिवो मे सप्तऋषीन् उपतिष्ठस्व \\ ऊर्ध्वं मे नाभेः सीद \ मा मे ऽवाङ् नाभिम् अतिगास् \\ इति गात्राणि सम्̐स्पृशन्ते ॥
9.12.m: They touch their limbs with: "Invigorate my limbs, O possessor of bay steeds! Graciously approach my seven seers! Settle above my navel! Pass not downwards beyond my navel!"
They touch the cups with the two [mantras beginning with]: "Swell up…"
Or they pour in soma, because [swelling up] with the mantra is impossible [otherwise].

9.12.s: asarvabhakṣāṃs tān dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasya paścādakṣaṃ nidadhati camasān adhaḥ //
9.12.d: असर्वभक्षांस् तान् दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्य पश्चादक्षं निदधति चमसान् अधः ॥
9.12.m: Those cups not entirely consumed, they deposit beneath, behind the axle of the southern Havirdhāna cart.
They are the Nārāśaṃsa [cups], up to the Vaiśvadeva [recitation].

9.12.s: puroḍāśaśakalam ādāya samupahūtāḥ smas \\ ity uktvottiṣṭhati //
9.12.d: पुरोडाशशकलम् आदाय समुपहूताः स्मस् \\ इत्य् उक्त्वोत्तिष्ठति ॥
9.12.m: Having taken a piece of the sacrificial cake and said: "We are invited," he stands up.

9.12.s: achāvākāyainat prayachann āha \\ achavāka vadasva yat te vādyam iti //
9.12.d: अछावाकायैनत् प्रयछन्न् आह \\ अछवाक वदस्व यत् ते वाद्यम् इति ॥
9.12.m: Handing it over to the Acchāvāka, he says: "Acchāvāka, speak what is to be spoken by thee!"

9.12.s: upo asmān iti bruvati hotāram āha \\ upahavam ayaṃ brāhmaṇa ichate \ tam̐ hotar upahvayasva \\ iti //
9.12.d: उपो अस्मान् इति ब्रुवति होतारम् आह \\ उपहवम् अयं ब्राह्मण इछते \ तम्̐ होतर् उपह्वयस्व \\ इति ॥
9.12.m: When he says: "[Invite] us…" he says to the Hotṛ: "This brāhmaṇa desires an invitation; Hotṛ, invite him!"
Being invited, he causes [the Hotṛ] to recite for [the soma] being drawn.
He draws the cup for the Acchāvāka.
Having performed everything up to the depositing in the manner of the Hotra-cups,
and [he is placed] earlier than the Āgnīdhra from now on.
In the Āgnīdhra shed the priests of the havis-sacrifice eat the iḍā.

9.13.s: droṇakalaśāt \\ upayāmagṛhīto 'si madhave tvā \\ iti dvādaśa pratimantram //
9.13.d: द्रोणकलशात् \\ उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि मधवे त्वा \\ इति द्वादश प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
9.13.m: From the droṇakalaśa trough, [they draw] twelve [cups], one per mantra, with 'You are taken with a base; for Madhu you [I take]' and so on.
Each preceding mantra belongs to the Adhvaryu;
each subsequent one belongs to the Pratiprasthātṛ.
Simultaneously they draw the first two,
and [they make] the offering of all of them [by alternation].
One steps out [to offer], while the other enters [to draw].
Each subsequent [offering] is made by the Pratiprasthātṛ, on account of his later turn.
Holding the vessel, he passes around the Adhvaryu on both sides.
[The offerings] prior to the last two are offered in their entirety (sarvahuta).
The two give the prompt six times with '[Worship] with the Season';
four times with 'with the Seasons', having reversed the mouth of the vessel;

9.13.s: yajamānaḥ preṣitas \\ hotar etad yaja \\ iti brūyāt //
9.13.d: यजमानः प्रेषितस् \\ होतर् एतद् यज \\ इति ब्रूयात् ॥
9.13.m: Being prompted, the sacrificer should say: 'Hotṛ priest, worship this!'

9.13.s: trayodaśaṃ gṛhṇīyād ichann upayāmagṛhīto 'sy am̐hasaspataye tvā \\ iti //
9.13.d: त्रयोदशं गृह्णीयाद् इछन्न् उपयामगृहीतो ऽस्य् अम्̐हसस्पतये त्वा \\ इति ॥
9.13.m: If he wishes, he may draw a thirteenth [cup] with 'You are taken with a base; for the Lord of Distress you [I take]'.
He offers [it] after the Pratiprasthātṛ.

9.13.s: anyatarasmiñ cheṣau kṛtvā vaśinaindrāgnaṃ gṛhṇāti pratiprasthātā \\ indrāgnī iti //
9.13.d: अन्यतरस्मिञ् छेषौ कृत्वा वशिनैन्द्राग्नं गृह्णाति प्रतिप्रस्थाता \\ इन्द्राग्नी इति ॥
9.13.m: Having placed the remnants in either [vessel], the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the Indrāgni cup with a wish-yielding [mantra], with 'Indra and Agni...';
he brings the portion for consumption (bhakṣa) to the Hotṛ, Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, Agnīdh, Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and Praśāstṛ priests.
[He does so] having reversed the vessel for the Hotṛ, Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, and Achāvāka.
As much as was stated [belongs] to the Hotṛ, on account of the sacrificer's connection, as in the case of the selection [of priests];
or the consumption by the Hotṛ is due to a specific rule;
Having reversed the vessel, the Hotṛ's consumption is twofold;
or only that much, because the preceding [cups] were offered entirely.

9.13.s: nirhṛtya pātram̐ hotuḥ purastāt prāṅ āste //
9.13.d: निर्हृत्य पात्रम्̐ होतुः पुरस्तात् प्राङ् आस्ते ॥
9.13.m: Having taken out the vessel, he sits facing east in front of the Hotṛ.

9.13.s: abhihutaḥ śom̐sāva \\ ity āvṛty *< othā modaiva \\ iti pratigṛṇāti praṇavāvasānayoḥ //
9.13.d: अभिहुतः शोम्̐साव \\ इत्य् आवृत्य् *< ओथा मोदैव \\ इति प्रतिगृणाति प्रणवावसानयोः ॥
9.13.m: Addressed by the Hotṛ with 'Having offered, let us two recite', he turns round and responds with 'othā modaiva' at the praṇavas (oṃ) and pauses;

9.13.s: aindrāgnam ādāyāśrāvyāha \\ ukthaśā yaja somasya \\ iti //
9.13.d: ऐन्द्राग्नम् आदायाश्राव्याह \\ उक्थशा यज सोमस्य \\ इति ॥
9.13.m: Having taken the Indrāgni cup and caused [the Agnīdh] to announce (āśrāvya), he says: 'Reciter of the uktha, worship for soma!'
This is the prompting formula (praiṣa) for the [offerings] accompanied by recitation.
And there is shaking of the Nārāśaṃsa cups while the offering is being poured.
If [they are] not yet deposited, the offering of the [cup] accompanied by recitation takes place.
Having performed [the rites] from the consumption up to the depositing,

9.14.s: vaiśvadevaṃ gṛhṇāti śukrapātreṇa droṇakalaśād anvārabdhe vā \\ omāsas \\ iti //
9.14.d: वैश्वदेवं गृह्णाति शुक्रपात्रेण द्रोणकलशाद् अन्वारब्धे वा \\ ओमासस् \\ इति ॥
9.14.m: he draws the Vaiśvadeva cup with the Śukra vessel from the droṇakalaśa, or while [the sacrificer] holds onto him, with 'You who protect...'.
Having poured the Śukra [soma] into the pūtabhṛt vessel, there is the joining of the droṇakalaśa and the strainer.
He parcels out the sacrificial cakes for the soma pressing (savanīya-puroḍāśas), beginning with the animal-cake, with the exception of the payasyā (curd offering).

9.14.s: stotram upākaroti tṛṇābhyāṃ graham upaspṛśya \\ upāvartadhvam iti //
9.14.d: स्तोत्रम् उपाकरोति तृणाभ्यां ग्रहम् उपस्पृश्य \\ उपावर्तध्वम् इति ॥
9.14.m: Having touched the soma cup with two blades of grass, he initiates the chant (stotra) with 'Turn yourselves toward [us]'.
The washing of the vessels takes place at the mārjālīya hearth.

9.14.s: ukthyaṃ vigṛhṇāti traidham \\ devebhyas tvā \\ iti sarvebhyaḥ //
9.14.d: उक्थ्यं विगृह्णाति त्रैधम् \\ देवेभ्यस् त्वा \\ इति सर्वेभ्यः ॥
9.14.m: He draws the Ukthya cup into three portions, for all [three assistant Hotṛs] with 'For the gods you [I take]';
or for the Praśāstṛ with 'For Mitra and Varuṇa you [I take]'.

9.14.d: उक्थशा यज सोमानाम् इति प्रैषो ऽनाराशम्̐सेषु ॥
9.14.m: 'Reciter of the uktha, worship for the somas' is the prompting formula in the case of the cups that are not Nārāśaṃsa.

9.14.s: yasya vigrahas tasya prathamaṃ camasam unnayati //
9.14.d: यस्य विग्रहस् तस्य प्रथमं चमसम् उन्नयति ॥
9.14.m: He draws up first the cup of that priest whose is the drawn portion (vigraha);
and into this [cup] he pours the residue of the soma cup.

9.14.s: evaṃ pratiprasthātottarābhyām indrāya tvā \\ iti brāhmaṇācham̐sine \\ indrāgnibhyāṃ tvā \\ ity achāvākāya //
9.14.d: एवं प्रतिप्रस्थातोत्तराभ्याम् इन्द्राय त्वा \\ इति ब्राह्मणाछम्̐सिने \\ इन्द्राग्निभ्यां त्वा \\ इत्य् अछावाकाय ॥
9.14.m: In the same manner, the Pratiprasthātṛ [draws] with the subsequent two [formulas]: 'For Indra you [I take]' for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, and 'For Indra and Agni you [I take]' for the Achāvāka.
Prior to the drawn portion for the Achāvāka, the bringing down of the soma takes place.

9.14.s: vasatīvaryardhaṃ cāsiñcaty ādhavanīye viśve devā maruta indro asmān \ asmin dvitīye savane na jahyuḥ \ āyuṣmantaḥ priyam eṣāṃ vadantas \\ vayaṃ devānām̐ sumatau syāma \\ iti //
9.14.d: वसतीवर्यर्धं चासिञ्चत्य् आधवनीये विश्वे देवा मरुत इन्द्रो अस्मान् \ अस्मिन् द्वितीये सवने न जह्युः \ आयुष्मन्तः प्रियम् एषां वदन्तस् \\ वयं देवानाम्̐ सुमतौ स्याम \\ इति ॥
9.14.m: And he pours half of the vasatīvarī water into the ādhavanīya trough with 'May all the gods, the Maruts, and Indra not abandon us / at this second pressing; / living long and speaking what is dear to them, / may we abide in the favor of the gods' [VS 7.34].

9.14.s: carite sarvaiḥ praśāstaḥ prasūhi \\ iti brūyāt //
9.14.d: चरिते सर्वैः प्रशास्तः प्रसूहि \\ इति ब्रूयात् ॥
9.14.m: When [the rite] has been performed by all, he should say: 'Praśāstṛ, impel!'

10.1.m: Beginning with the creeping, the Midday soma pressing (mādhyandina-savana) takes place.
Having put vasatīvarī water into the Hotṛ's cup, he hands it to the sacrificer.
Beginning with taking up the pressing-stone, he performs the pressings in three rounds.
Because there is a scriptural statement that the Upām̐śusavana stone is not moved.
"Ihâ3, ihâ3" is the first round.
In place of "without pause", in the last [round he recites] "bṛhat, bṛhat".
Or [he presses only] half, because of the general instruction.
The drawing of the four cups begins with the Śukra cup.
The Āgrayaṇa cup [is drawn] from streams that form one-third of its own [allotment].

10.1.s: prāg ukthyān marutvatīyam ṛtupātreṇa \\ indra marutvas \\ iti //
10.1.d: प्राग् उक्थ्यान् मरुत्वतीयम् ऋतुपात्रेण \\ इन्द्र मरुत्वस् \\ इति ॥
10.1.m: Before the Ukthya cup, [he draws] the Marutvatīya cup with the season-cup, with the mantra: "Indra, accompanied by the Maruts..."

10.1.s: samanvārabdhaniṣkramaṇādi karoty ā \\ agnīd agnīn iti praiṣāt //
10.1.d: समन्वारब्धनिष्क्रमणादि करोत्य् आ \\ अग्नीद् अग्नीन् इति प्रैषात् ॥
10.1.m: He performs [the rites] beginning with stepping out while holding on to one another, up to the call: "Agnīdh, [kindle] the fires!"
The introduction of the Pavamāna chant takes place in the Sadas.
And in an Ahargaṇa sacrifice, everywhere, except at the Prāyaṇīya and Udayanīya days.

10.1.s: paśunehi \\ ity apakṛṣya dadhigharmāya dadhy āhara \ dakṣiṇā upāvartaya \\ iti praiṣopacayaḥ //
10.1.d: पशुनेहि \\ इत्य् अपकृष्य दधिघर्माय दध्य् आहर \ दक्षिणा उपावर्तय \\ इति प्रैषोपचयः ॥
10.1.m: Having postponed "Come here with the animal!", there is an addition of calls: "Bring the curds for the Dadhigharma!" and "Bring up the sacrificial gifts!"
The Dadhigharma offering is [performed] when there is a Pravargya rite.

10.1.s: upaviśya sadasaḥ purastāt sapavitrāyām agnihotrahavaṇyāṃ grahaṇaṃ yathoktam //
10.1.d: उपविश्य सदसः पुरस्तात् सपवित्रायाम् अग्निहोत्रहवण्यां ग्रहणं यथोक्तम् ॥
10.1.m: Sitting down to the east of the Sadas, the drawing [of the Dadhigharma] into the Agnihotrahavaṇī ladle with a strainer takes place as prescribed.

10.1.s: hotar vadasva yat te vādyam ity āha //
10.1.d: होतर् वदस्व यत् ते वाद्यम् इत्य् आह ॥
10.1.m: He says: "Hotṛ, recite what is to be recited by you!"

10.1.s: vādyānte śrātam̐ havir ity uttiṣṭhann āha //
10.1.d: वाद्यान्ते श्रातम्̐ हविर् इत्य् उत्तिष्ठन्न् आह ॥
10.1.m: At the end of the recitation, rising, he says: "The oblation is cooked!"
He calls: "Recite the offering verse for the Dadhigharma!"

10.1.s: hutaśeṣaṃ gharmartvijaḥ sayajamānāḥ samupahāvaṃ bhakṣayanti yathoktam //
10.1.d: हुतशेषं घर्मर्त्विजः सयजमानाः समुपहावं भक्षयन्ति यथोक्तम् ॥
10.1.m: The Gharma priests together with the sacrificer consume the remainder of the oblation after mutual invitation, as prescribed.
Or those who are uninitiated consume it by smelling.

10.1.s: paśupuroḍāśena pracarya puroḍāśādi karoty ā dhiṣṇyanidhānāt //
10.1.d: पशुपुरोडाशेन प्रचर्य पुरोडाशादि करोत्य् आ धिष्ण्यनिधानात् ॥
10.1.m: Having performed the offering of the animal cake, he performs [the rites] beginning with the cakes up to the placing of the dhiṣṇya hearths.
And beginning with the preparatory call for the portions being drawn up, until the placing of the cups.

10.2.s: madhyandinasya savanasya niṣkevalyasya bhāgasya śukravato madhuścuta indrāya somān prasthitān preṣya \\ iti //
10.2.d: मध्यन्दिनस्य सवनस्य निष्केवल्यस्य भागस्य शुक्रवतो मधुश्चुत इन्द्राय सोमान् प्रस्थितान् प्रेष्य \\ इति ॥
10.2.m: [The call is]: "For the midday soma pressing, for the Niṣkevalya share, accompanied by the Śukra cup, dripping with sweetness, urge the soma offerings set forth for Indra!"
Or "accompanied by the Manthin cup" in place of "dripping with sweetness".
Having consumed the iḍā portion, the Dākṣiṇa oblation [is offered] in the Śālādvārya fire.

10.2.s: vāsaḥprabaddham̐ hiraṇyam̐ havanyām avadhāya caturgṛhītam ud u tyam iti //
10.2.d: वासःप्रबद्धम्̐ हिरण्यम्̐ हवन्याम् अवधाय चतुर्गृहीतम् उद् उ त्यम् इति ॥
10.2.m: Having placed into the offering ladle gold tied in a cloth, [he offers] a fourfold-scooped [oblation with the mantra]: "Up that [all-knowing god]..."
The second [oblation with the mantra]: "The wonderful [face of the gods]..."
In the Āgnīdhra fire, with: "O Agni, lead [us]..."

10.2.s: ayaṃ nas \\ ity aparām aśvaṃ ced yuktaṃ dadyād ayuktaṃ vā //
10.2.d: अयं नस् \\ इत्य् अपराम् अश्वं चेद् युक्तं दद्याद् अयुक्तं वा ॥
10.2.m: Another [oblation with]: "This our [brother]...", if he should give a horse, whether harnessed or unharnessed.

10.2.s: sahiraṇyo yajamānaḥ śālāṃ pūrveṇa tiṣṭhann abhimantrayate dakṣiṇā bahirvedi tiṣṭhatīr dakṣiṇatas \\ rūpeṇa vas \\ iti //
10.2.d: सहिरण्यो यजमानः शालां पूर्वेण तिष्ठन्न् अभिमन्त्रयते दक्षिणा बहिर्वेदि तिष्ठतीर् दक्षिणतस् \\ रूपेण वस् \\ इति ॥
10.2.m: The sacrificer, holding gold, standing to the east of the sacrificial hall, addresses the sacrificial gifts standing to the south outside the altar with: "By your form..."
A hundred cows or twelve cross over.
And churned drink, boiled rice, sesame, and beans.
Between the sacrificial hall and the Sadas, south of the Āgnīdhra hearth, along the proper path.
And he optionally calls the Subrahmaṇyā recitation.
He follows from the Āgnīdhra hearth, pressing.
He goes to the Sadas with: "O wide light..."
He looks at the members of the assembly with: "Strive together with the members of the assembly!"
The going to the Āgnīdhra fire [is performed] with: "Today the brāhmaṇa..."

10.2.s: upaviśya hiraṇyam asmai dadāti \\ asmadrātās \\ iti //
10.2.d: उपविश्य हिरण्यम् अस्मै ददाति \\ अस्मद्रातास् \\ इति ॥
10.2.m: Having sat down, he gives him gold with: "Given by us..."

10.2.s: ātreyāya cāgnīdhravat sadasaḥ purastād upaviṣṭāya ka ātreyaṃ ka ātreyam iti trir uktvā sakṛcheṣam ahāleyam avāleyam akaudreyam aśaubhreyam avāmarathyam agaupavanam iti //
10.2.d: आत्रेयाय चाग्नीध्रवत् सदसः पुरस्ताद् उपविष्टाय क आत्रेयं क आत्रेयम् इति त्रिर् उक्त्वा सकृछेषम् अहालेयम् अवालेयम् अकौद्रेयम् अशौभ्रेयम् अवामरथ्यम् अगौपवनम् इति ॥
10.2.m: And to an Ātreya, seated to the east of the Sadas, just like to the Āgnīdh, having said three times: "Who is an Ātreya? Who is an Ātreya?", [he gives gold] once, with the remainder: "free from Hala, free from Vala, free from Kudra, free from Śobhra, free from Vāmaratha, free from Gopavana".
He gives the sacrificial gifts to the officiating priests.
Hundreds individually according to the distinction of persons.
Or there is apportionment according to the primacy of the duties.

10.2.s: yathārambhaṃ dvādaśadvādaśādyebhyaḥ ṣaṭṣaḍ dvitīyebhyaś catasraścatasras tṛtīyebhyas tisrastisra itarebhyaḥ //
10.2.d: यथारम्भं द्वादशद्वादशाद्येभ्यः षट्षड् द्वितीयेभ्यश् चतस्रश्चतस्रस् तृतीयेभ्यस् तिस्रस्तिस्र इतरेभ्यः ॥
10.2.m: According to the starting order: twelve each to the first, six each to the second, four each to the third, and three each to the others.
[First] to the Brahman, Udgātṛ, and Hotṛ.
And to the two Adhvaryu priests seated in the Havirdhāna shed.
The two receive the gold with: "To Agni thee..."
The cloth with: "To Bṛhaspati thee..."
Having returned, [he gives gifts] to the Prastotṛ, Praśāstṛ, Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, Potṛ, Neṣṭṛ, Acchāvāka, Unnetṛ, Grāvastut, and Subrahmaṇya.
And [he gives] other [gifts] to those who have glided forward, except to Kaṇvas, Kaśyapas, and beggars.

10.2.s: na rajataṃ dadyād barhiṣi purāsya saṃvatsarād gṛhe rudantīti śruteḥ //
10.2.d: न रजतं दद्याद् बर्हिषि पुरास्य संवत्सराद् गृहे रुदन्तीति श्रुतेः ॥
10.2.m: He should not give silver upon the sacrificial grass, because of the Vedic text: 'They weep in his house before a year [passes].'
Having given to all, [he gives] to the Pratihartṛ afterwards.

10.3.m: He causes [the Hotṛ] to recite for Indra accompanied by the Maruts.

10.3.s: ṛtupātreṇa marutvatīyagrahaṇam upayāmagṛhīto 'si marutāṃ tvaujase \\ iti //
10.3.d: ऋतुपात्रेण मरुत्वतीयग्रहणम् उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि मरुतां त्वौजसे \\ इति ॥
10.3.m: Drawing of the Marutvatīya cup with the seasonal cup, with: 'You are taken with a support; for the strength of the Maruts you...;'

10.3.s: adhvaryum anu juhoti saśastre tv ānupūrvyayogāt //
10.3.d: अध्वर्युम् अनु जुहोति सशस्त्रे त्व् आनुपूर्व्ययोगात् ॥
10.3.m: He offers after the Adhvaryu; but where there is a recitation, on account of proper sequence,
Drawing of the Marutvatīya cup with the ruler cup, with: 'Accompanied by the Maruts...'
When the cup has been carried out, the Hotṛ recites.

10.3.s: janiṣṭhā ugras \\ ity etasyām \\ madā modaiva \\ iti pratigaraḥ sakṛt //
10.3.d: जनिष्ठा उग्रस् \\ इत्य् एतस्याम् \\ मदा मोदैव \\ इति प्रतिगरः सकृत् ॥
10.3.m: At the verse 'The fierce one was born...,' the response is once: 'Rejoice, delight!'

10.3.s: ā nidhānāt kṛtvā māhendraṃ gṛhṇāti vaiśvadevavat \\ mahā3ṃ indras \\ iti //
10.3.d: आ निधानात् कृत्वा माहेन्द्रं गृह्णाति वैश्वदेववत् \\ महा3ं इन्द्रस् \\ इति ॥
10.3.m: Having performed [the rites] up to the setting down [of the cup], he draws the Māhendra cup in the same manner as the Vaiśvadeva cup, with: 'Indra is great...'

10.3.s: śukraṃ pūtabhṛty āsicya pṛṣṭham upākṛtya preṣyati \\ abhiṣotāro 'bhiṣuṇuta \\ aulūkhalān udvādayata \\ agnīd āśiraṃ vinaya \ saumyasya vittāt \\ iti //
10.3.d: शुक्रं पूतभृत्य् आसिच्य पृष्ठम् उपाकृत्य प्रेष्यति \\ अभिषोतारो ऽभिषुणुत \\ औलूखलान् उद्वादयत \\ अग्नीद् आशिरं विनय \ सौम्यस्य वित्तात् \\ इति ॥
10.3.m: Having poured the pure soma into the Pūtabhṛt vat and initiated the Pṛṣṭha chant, he issues the call: 'Pressers, press! Make the mortars resound! Agnīdh, mix the milk! Know what belongs to Soma!'

10.3.s: ṛjīṣamiśram am̐śum abhiṣunvanti yathā kathā cānudakam //
10.3.d: ऋजीषमिश्रम् अम्̐शुम् अभिषुन्वन्ति यथा कथा चानुदकम् ॥
10.3.m: They press the soma stalk mixed with the pressed-out residue in any manner whatsoever, without water.
because of the instruction for repeated pressing in three rounds;
omitting measuring and touching, because they have already been done;
and purifying into the Pūtabhṛt vat, because there is no pure soma.
While the chant is being sung, the pressed-out residue is put into the Kubha;
the mess of boiled rice for Soma and the single-potsherd cake for Varuṇa are additional.

10.3.s: ā pātraprakṣālanāt kṛtvokthyaṃ vigṛhṇāti pūrvavat \\ indrāya tvā \\ iti sarvebhyaḥ //
10.3.d: आ पात्रप्रक्षालनात् कृत्वोक्थ्यं विगृह्णाति पूर्ववत् \\ इन्द्राय त्वा \\ इति सर्वेभ्यः ॥
10.3.m: Having performed [the rites] up to the washing of the cups, he portions out the Ukthya cup as before, with: 'For Indra you...,' from all [the cups].

10.3.s: vasatīvarīś cāsiñcati \\ idaṃ tṛtīyasavanaṃ kavīnām \ ṛtena ye camasam airayanta \ te saudhanvanāḥ svar ānaśānāḥ \ sviṣṭiṃ no 'bhi vasīyo nayantu \\ iti //
10.3.d: वसतीवरीश् चासिञ्चति \\ इदं तृतीयसवनं कवीनाम् \ ऋतेन ये चमसम् ऐरयन्त \ ते सौधन्वनाः स्वर् आनशानाः \ स्विष्टिं नो ऽभि वसीयो नयन्तु \\ इति ॥
10.3.m: And he pours the Vasatīvarī waters, with: 'This third pressing belongs to the sages, who stirred the cup through the cosmic order; may those sons of Sudhanvan, having attained heaven, lead our well-performed sacrifice to greater wealth.'

10.4.m: The Adhvaryu, the sacrificer, the Pratiprasthātṛ, the Agnīdh, and the Unnetṛ enter the Havirdhāna cart-shed,

10.4.s: apihitadvāra ādityapātram ādāya sam̐sravāṃś copari pūtabhṛtas tata ādityagrahaṃ gṛhṇāti sam̐sravebhyaḥ kadā cana \\ iti //
10.4.d: अपिहितद्वार आदित्यपात्रम् आदाय सम्̐स्रवांश् चोपरि पूतभृतस् तत आदित्यग्रहं गृह्णाति सम्̐स्रवेभ्यः कदा चन \\ इति ॥
10.4.m: While the door is closed, taking the Āditya vessel and the dregs over the Pūtabhṛt vat, he then draws the Āditya cup from the dregs, with: 'Never...;'

10.4.s: dadhnā śrīṇāty enaṃ paścime 'nte madhye vā yajño devānām iti //
10.4.d: दध्ना श्रीणात्य् एनं पश्चिमे ऽन्ते मध्ये वा यज्ञो देवानाम् इति ॥
10.4.m: he mixes it with curds at the western end or in the middle, with: 'The sacrifice of the gods...;'
he stirs it with the Upām̐śusavana pressing stone, with: 'O brilliant Āditya...;'
he hands the Upām̐śusavana stone to the Unnetṛ,

10.4.s: ādhavanīye camase vā somavati grāvṇo 'vadhāya sthāne nidadhāti //
10.4.d: आधवनीये चमसे वा सोमवति ग्राव्णो ऽवधाय स्थाने निदधाति ॥
10.4.m: Having placed the pressing stones into the Ādhavanīya trough or into a cup containing soma, he deposits them in their place.

10.4.s: apāvṛtadvāre niṣkrāmato graham apidhāya pāṇinā sthālyā vānvārabdhe //
10.4.d: अपावृतद्वारे निष्क्रामतो ग्रहम् अपिधाय पाणिना स्थाल्या वान्वारब्धे ॥
10.4.m: When the door is opened, both of them step out, covering the cup with a hand or with a bowl, while they maintain contact,

10.4.s: praiṣānuvācanayor anyatarasminn āha priyebhyaḥ priyadhāmabhyaḥ priyavratebhyo maha svasarasya patibhya uror antarikṣasyādhyakṣebhyas \\ iti //
10.4.d: प्रैषानुवाचनयोर् अन्यतरस्मिन्न् आह प्रियेभ्यः प्रियधामभ्यः प्रियव्रतेभ्यो मह स्वसरस्य पतिभ्य उरोर् अन्तरिक्षस्याध्यक्षेभ्यस् \\ इति ॥
10.4.m: In either the call or the invitation to recite, he says: 'To the dear ones, who have dear abodes, who observe dear vows, to the lords of the great resting-place, to the overseers of the wide atmosphere...'
Having offered, he hands the two remnants to the Pratiprasthātṛ.
Here takes place the gliding, because of the Vedic text [placing it] before the Āditya cup at the third pressing.

10.5.s: āgrāyaṇam ādāyāsiñcati pavitre 'dhipūtabhṛtaṃ pratiprasthātā ca sam̐sravāv ādhavanīyād unnetodañcanena camasena vā tata āgrāyaṇaṃ gṛhṇāti //
10.5.d: आग्रायणम् आदायासिञ्चति पवित्रे ऽधिपूतभृतं प्रतिप्रस्थाता च सम्̐स्रवाव् आधवनीयाद् उन्नेतोदञ्चनेन चमसेन वा तत आग्रायणं गृह्णाति ॥
10.5.m: Taking the Āgrāyaṇa vessel, he pours [soma] over the strainer placed upon the Pūtabhṛt vat, and the Pratiprasthātṛ [pours] the two remnants; the Unnetṛ [pours soma] from the Ādhavanīya trough with a ladle or a cup; then he draws the Āgrāyaṇa cup.
And the Ukthya cup at the subsequent ones with a single [drawing].

10.5.s: pūtabhṛty āśiram āsiñcati \\ āśīr ma ūrjam uta suprajāstvam \ iṣaṃ dadhātu draviṇam̐ suvarcasam \ saṃjayan kṣetrāṇi sahasāham indra \ kṛṇvāno 'nyān adharānt sapatnān iti //
10.5.d: पूतभृत्य् आशिरम् आसिञ्चति \\ आशीर् म ऊर्जम् उत सुप्रजास्त्वम् \ इषं दधातु द्रविणम्̐ सुवर्चसम् \ संजयन् क्षेत्राणि सहसाहम् इन्द्र \ कृण्वानो ऽन्यान् अधरान्त् सपत्नान् इति ॥
10.5.m: He pours the warm milk into the Pūtabhṛt vat, with: 'May the warm milk bestow upon me vigor and noble offspring, nourishment, wealth, and splendid luster; conquering fields by force, O Indra, casting down other rivals.'

10.5.s: śrad asmai naras \\ ity enam avekṣate patnī //
10.5.d: श्रद् अस्मै नरस् \\ इत्य् एनम् अवेक्षते पत्नी ॥
10.5.m: The wife gazes at it, with: 'Trusting in him, O men...'
He performs the stepping out in contact and the other rites as at the midday pressing.
In place of the piling up [of cake pieces], [he says]: 'Converse over the victim.'

10.5.s: prātaḥsavanaprabhṛty ā saṃvādāchruteḥ śamitranuśāsanaprabhṛtīḍāntaṃ kṛtvā puroḍāśādi ceḍābhakṣāt //
10.5.d: प्रातःसवनप्रभृत्य् आ संवादाछ्रुतेः शमित्रनुशासनप्रभृतीडान्तं कृत्वा पुरोडाशादि चेडाभक्षात् ॥
10.5.m: From the morning pressing up to the conversation, according to the Vedic text; having performed from the instruction to the slaughterer up to the Iḍā, and the sacrificial cake and other rites up to the consumption of the Iḍā,

10.5.s: hotṛcamasaṃ gṛhītvāśrāvyāha tṛtīyasya savanasya ṛbhumato vibhumato vājavato bṛhaspatimato viśvadevyāvatas tīvrā3ṃ āśīrvata indrāya somān prasthitān preṣya \\ iti //
10.5.d: होतृचमसं गृहीत्वाश्राव्याह तृतीयस्य सवनस्य ऋभुमतो विभुमतो वाजवतो बृहस्पतिमतो विश्वदेव्यावतस् तीव्रा3ं आशीर्वत इन्द्राय सोमान् प्रस्थितान् प्रेष्य \\ इति ॥
10.5.m: Having taken the Hotṛ's cup and caused [the Agnīdh] to announce, he says: 'Urge the soma portions set out for Indra of the third pressing, who is accompanied by the Ṛbhus, accompanied by the Vibhus, accompanied by Vāja, accompanied by Bṛhaspati, accompanied by the Viśvedevas, sharp, accompanied by milk!'
'Accompanied by milk' in place of 'pure soma.'

10.5.s: grāg iḍābhakṣād dhavirdhāne yathāsvaṃ camaseṣūpāsyanti puroḍāśamātrā anudakāḥ piṇḍapitṛyajñavad dānaprabhṛti prāg avaghrāṇāt //
10.5.d: ग्राग् इडाभक्षाद् धविर्धाने यथास्वं चमसेषूपास्यन्ति पुरोडाशमात्रा अनुदकाः पिण्डपितृयज्ञवद् दानप्रभृति प्राग् अवघ्राणात् ॥
10.5.m: Before the consumption of the Iḍā, in the Havirdhāna cart-shed, into their respective cups, they cast portions of the sacrificial cake without water, as in the Piṇḍapitṛyajña, from the giving onward, prior to smelling;
or to the ancestors of the sacrificer, because of his eligibility for the fruit.

10.5.s: bhakṣayitveḍām upām̐śvantaryāmapātrayor anyatareṇa sāvitragrahaṇam \\ vāmam adya \\ iti //
10.5.d: भक्षयित्वेडाम् उपाम्̐श्वन्तर्यामपात्रयोर् अन्यतरेण सावित्रग्रहणम् \\ वामम् अद्य \\ इति ॥
10.5.m: Having eaten the Iḍā, drawing of the Sāvitra cup with either of the two vessels, the Upām̐śu or the Antaryāma, with: 'A fair [gift] today...;'
at the proper time, the Pātnīvata cup with the other.

10.6.m: He causes [the Hotṛ] to recite for the god Savitṛ.

10.6.d: अभक्षितेन महावैश्वदेवग्रहणम् उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि सुशर्मासि \\ इति ॥
10.6.m: With [the cup] from which has not been consumed, drawing of the Mahāvaiśvadeva cup, with: 'You are taken with a support; you are well-sheltering...;'

10.6.s: ekayā ca daśabhiś ca \\ iti śasyamāne dvidevatyāni pratiprasthātā prakṣālya khare nidadhāti //
10.6.d: एकया च दशभिश् च \\ इति शस्यमाने द्विदेवत्यानि प्रतिप्रस्थाता प्रक्षाल्य खरे निदधाति ॥
10.6.m: While the verse "With one and with ten..." is being recited, the Pratiprasthātṛ, having washed the cups for two deities, places them on the mound.

10.6.s: pra dyāvā yajñair ity etāsu madā modaiva \\ iti triḥ pratigaraḥ //
10.6.d: प्र द्यावा यज्ञैर् इत्य् एतासु मदा मोदैव \\ इति त्रिः प्रतिगरः ॥
10.6.m: During the verses "Forward, O Heaven and Earth, with sacrifices...", "Indeed, great joy!" is the response thrice.
And during the verses beginning with "Indeed sweet..." if he wishes.
Having performed [the rites] up to the washing of the vessels, he proceeds with the Soma offering to Soma.
He surrounds it with yajati-offerings of clarified butter on both sides.

10.6.s: ghṛtasya yaja \\ ity āha ghṛtaśabda upām̐śu //
10.6.d: घृतस्य यज \\ इत्य् आह घृतशब्द उपाम्̐शु ॥
10.6.m: He says: "Recite the yājyā verse for the clarified butter," with the word "clarified butter" muttered softly.
Saying: "Recite the yājyā verse for the Soma offering," when proceeding with the Soma offering.
[He follows the ritual] as prescribed, down to the drawing again of the Soma cup.
Having poured clarified butter, he hands the Soma offering over to the Udgātṛ.

10.6.s: caturgṛhītaṃ pracaraṇyā dhiṣṇyeṣu juhoti yathānyuptaṃ prabhāvayañ chālākān pradīpyapradīpya vibhūr asi \\ iti pratimantram //
10.6.d: चतुर्गृहीतं प्रचरण्या धिष्ण्येषु जुहोति यथान्युप्तं प्रभावयञ् छालाकान् प्रदीप्यप्रदीप्य विभूर् असि \\ इति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
10.6.m: He offers four ladlings [of clarified butter] with the pracaraṇī ladle onto the hearths in the order they were strewn, causing the splinters to catch fire by lighting them one by one, with the respective mantra: "You are all-pervading..."
On the Āgnīdhra hearth again from behind, if he wishes.

10.6.s: upayāmagṛhīto 'si bṛhaspatisutasya \\ iti pratiprasthātā pātnīvataṃ gṛhṇāti //
10.6.d: उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि बृहस्पतिसुतस्य \\ इति प्रतिप्रस्थाता पात्नीवतं गृह्णाति ॥
10.6.m: With "You are taken with a support; of that which is pressed by Bṛhaspati...", the Pratiprasthātṛ draws the Pātnīvata cup.

10.6.s: pracaraṇīśeṣeṇa śrīṇāty enam ahaṃ parastāt \\ iti //
10.6.d: प्रचरणीशेषेण श्रीणात्य् एनम् अहं परस्तात् \\ इति ॥
10.6.m: With the residue in the pracaraṇī ladle, he mixes it, with "Him I [anoint] beyond..."
He says: "Agnīdh, recite the yājyā verse for the Pātnīvata cup."
He offers in the northern half [of the fire] with: "O Agni, possessor of wives!"

10.6.s: preṣyati ca \\ agnīn neṣṭur upastham āsīda \ neṣṭaḥ patnīm udānaya \\ udgātrā saṃkhyāpaya \\ unnetar hotuś camasam anūnnaya somaṃ mātirīricas \\ iti //
10.6.d: प्रेष्यति च \\ अग्नीन् नेष्टुर् उपस्थम् आसीद \ नेष्टः पत्नीम् उदानय \\ उद्गात्रा संख्यापय \\ उन्नेतर् होतुश् चमसम् अनून्नय सोमं मातिरीरिचस् \\ इति ॥
10.6.m: And he commands: "Agnīdh, sit in the lap of the Neṣṭṛ; Neṣṭṛ, bring up the wife; make her gaze at the Udgātṛ; Unnetṛ, fill up the Hotṛ's cup, do not leave any soma behind!"
"Make [the soma] abundant!" [is the command] in the Ukthya and subsequent sacrifices.
The consumption [takes place] in the Āgnīdhra shed with the vaṣaṭ-call and the invitation.
With the vessel, he sits down in the lap of the Neṣṭṛ.
Or the consumption takes place here, on account of the fitness of bringing the vessel.
Having washed the vessel, the Agnīdh places it on the mound.

10.7.m: Having touched the Hotṛ's cup, he introduces the Yajñāyajñīya chant.
And he covers his head if he wishes, like the Udgātṛ.

10.7.s: patnīm̐ sadaḥ praveśyāpareṇottarata upaviṣṭāmudgātrā samīkṣayati prajāpatir vṛṣāsi \\ iti //
10.7.d: पत्नीम्̐ सदः प्रवेश्यापरेणोत्तरत उपविष्टामुद्गात्रा समीक्षयति प्रजापतिर् वृषासि \\ इति ॥
10.7.m: Having brought the wife into the Sadas and made her sit behind towards the north, he makes her look at the Udgātṛ with: "Prajāpati, you are a male..."
Having uncovered her right thigh, he sprinkles her with water for washing the feet.
Permitted by the Udgātṛ, she departs.

10.7.s: evā na indro maghavā \\ iti śasyamāne dhruvam̐ hotṛcamase 'vanayati dhruvaṃ dhruveṇa \\ iti //
10.7.d: एवा न इन्द्रो मघवा \\ इति शस्यमाने ध्रुवम्̐ होतृचमसे ऽवनयति ध्रुवं ध्रुवेण \\ इति ॥
10.7.m: While "Thus indeed Indra, the bounteous..." is being recited, he pours the Dhruva cup into the Hotṛ's cup with: "Firm with the firm..."
Or [using] "I take" in place of "I pour".
If the Vaiśvānara cup was drawn, [it is poured into the cup] of the sacrificer.
At the conclusion of the washing of the vessels, the after-offerings [take place], beginning with the kindling stick.

10.7.s: ukthyavigrahaṇam uttareṣu \\ indrāvaruṇābhyām \ indrābṛhaspatibhyām \ indrāviṣṇubhyām iti //
10.7.d: उक्थ्यविग्रहणम् उत्तरेषु \\ इन्द्रावरुणाभ्याम् \ इन्द्राबृहस्पतिभ्याम् \ इन्द्राविष्णुभ्याम् इति ॥
10.7.m: In the subsequent [forms of sacrifice], there is the drawing of the Ukthya cups: "For Indra and Varuṇa," "For Indra and Bṛhaspati," and "For Indra and Viṣṇu."
If it is a Ṣoḍaśin, there are an additional chant and recitation.
At the third pressing, there is no generation [of new cups].

10.7.s: srugvyūhanam agner vanaspater indrasya vasumato rudravata ādityavata ṛbhumato vibhumato vājavato bṛhaspatimato viśvadevyāvataḥ somasyojjitim iti \\ agnir vanaspatir indro vasumān rudravān ādityavān ṛbhumān vibhumān vājavān bṛhaspatimān viśvadevyāvānt somas tam apanudantu \\ iti //
10.7.d: स्रुग्व्यूहनम् अग्नेर् वनस्पतेर् इन्द्रस्य वसुमतो रुद्रवत आदित्यवत ऋभुमतो विभुमतो वाजवतो बृहस्पतिमतो विश्वदेव्यावतः सोमस्योज्जितिम् इति \\ अग्निर् वनस्पतिर् इन्द्रो वसुमान् रुद्रवान् आदित्यवान् ऋभुमान् विभुमान् वाजवान् बृहस्पतिमान् विश्वदेव्यावान्त् सोमस् तम् अपनुदन्तु \\ इति ॥
10.7.m: The separation of the two ladles is done with: "The winning of Agni, of Vanaspati, of Indra accompanied by the Vasus, accompanied by the Rudras, accompanied by the Ādityas, accompanied by the Ṛbhus, accompanied by the Vibhus, accompanied by the Vājas, accompanied by Bṛhaspati, accompanied by the Viśvedevas, of Soma..." / "Let Agni, Vanaspati, Indra accompanied by the Vasus, accompanied by the Rudras, accompanied by the Ādityas, accompanied by the Ṛbhus, accompanied by the Vibhus, accompanied by the Vājas, accompanied by Bṛhaspati, accompanied by the Viśvedevas, and Soma cast him away!"
Or [only] with the deity of the victim and Vanaspati, because of the instruction [concerning] soma for the others.
Or all of them, because of the presence of the savanīya cake and the Soma offering.

10.8.s: vimucya srucau droṇakalaśe hāriyojanagrahaṇam upayāmagṛhīto 'si harir asi \\ iti //
10.8.d: विमुच्य स्रुचौ द्रोणकलशे हारियोजनग्रहणम् उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि हरिर् असि \\ इति ॥
10.8.m: Having unyoked the two ladles, he draws the Hāriyojana cup from the droṇakalaśa trough with: "You are taken with a support; you are the bay..."
And he throws in roasted grains with: "The roasted grains of the two bay steeds..."

10.8.s: unnetānuvācayati mūrdhani kṛtvā dhānāsomebhyo 'nubrūhi \\ ity āśrāvyāha dhānāsomān prasthitān preṣya \\ iti //
10.8.d: उन्नेतानुवाचयति मूर्धनि कृत्वा धानासोमेभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहि \\ इत्य् आश्राव्याह धानासोमान् प्रस्थितान् प्रेष्य \\ इति ॥
10.8.m: Having placed [the vessel] on his head, the Unnetṛ causes [the Hotṛ] to recite: "Recite for the soma with roasted grains"; and having called for the response, he says: "Prompt for the soma with roasted grains set out!"

10.8.s: uttaravedau vā nidhāya vilābham \\ yas te aśvasanir iti prāṇabhakṣaṃ bhakṣayitvottaravedau nivapanti //
10.8.d: उत्तरवेदौ वा निधाय विलाभम् \\ यस् ते अश्वसनिर् इति प्राणभक्षं भक्षयित्वोत्तरवेदौ निवपन्ति ॥
10.8.m: Or having placed it on the high altar, distributing it; having consumed it by inhalation with: "You who bestow horses...", they scatter it on the high altar.
The placing of the splinters with the respective mantra: "Of the god-made [sin]..."

10.8.s: apareṇa cātvālaṃ yathāsvaṃ camasān pūrṇapātrān avamṛśanti haritakuśān avadhāya saṃ varcasā \\ iti //
10.8.d: अपरेण चात्वालं यथास्वं चमसान् पूर्णपात्रान् अवमृशन्ति हरितकुशान् अवधाय सं वर्चसा \\ इति ॥
10.8.m: West of the Cātvāla pit, having inserted fresh kuśa grass, they touch their respective full cups with: "Together with lustre..."
The consumption of curds in the Āgnīdhra shed is with: "Of Dadhikrāvan..."
The Patnīsaṃyājas are like those of the animal sacrifice.

10.8.s: sam indra ṇas \\ iti nava samiṣṭayajūm̐ṣi juhoti pratimantram //
10.8.d: सम् इन्द्र णस् \\ इति नव समिष्टयजूम्̐षि जुहोति प्रतिमन्त्रम् ॥
10.8.m: He offers the nine samiṣṭayajus oblations, each with its respective mantra, beginning with: "Together, O Indra, with us..."
They carry the seat, the Udumbara staff, and whatever is smeared with soma to the Cātvāla pit.

10.8.s: kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāmekhale cātvāle prāsyati māhir bhūr iti //
10.8.d: कृष्णविषाणामेखले चात्वाले प्रास्यति माहिर् भूर् इति ॥
10.8.m: He throws the black antelope horn and the girdle into the Cātvāla pit with: "Do not become a snake!"
And the Pratiprasthātṛ [throws] the peg and the yoke-halter silently.

10.8.s: sāma preṣyati gāya \ brūhi \\ iti vā //
10.8.d: साम प्रेष्यति गाय \ ब्रूहि \\ इति वा ॥
10.8.m: He commands the sāman: "Sing!" or "Chant!"
All join in the finale.
Taking what was brought, they go to the purifying bath, to standing bodies of flowing waters.

10.8.d: नमो वरुणाय \\ इति वाचयत्य् अपो ऽवक्रमयन् ॥
10.8.m: Causing [the sacrificer] to step into the water, he makes him recite: "Homage to Varuṇa!"
