10.8.s: prāsya samidhaṃ caturgṛhītenābhijuhoti \\ agner anīkam iti //
10.8.d: प्रास्य समिधं चतुर्गृहीतेनाभिजुहोति \\ अग्नेर् अनीकम् इति ॥
10.8.m: Having thrown in a kindling stick, he offers over it with four ladlings [of clarified butter], with: "The face of Agni..."
[The oblations are made] behind, [namely] the fore-offerings excluding the barhis.
He performs the cutting [of portions] with the single-potsherd [cake].
If he wishes, he may cut a portion of the dregs of soma.
To Agni and Varuṇa the rest is offered entirely.
And once of the dregs of soma, if [taken] in the former [offering].
There are the two ghee portions and two after-offerings excluding the barhis, as spoken by the sacrificer.

10.9.m: he floats the jar of soma dregs with: 'In the ocean your [heart...]…'
Releasing it, he attends [the waters] with: 'O divine waters…'
He immerses it with: 'O bath (avabhṛtha)…'

10.9.s: kṛṣṇājināntaṃ ca mā maindryaṃ jyaiṣṭhyam̐ śraiṣṭhyaṃ vyauṣīr iti putrāyainat pradāya varuṇapraghāsavat snānaprabhṛy ā samidādhānāt //
10.9.d: कृष्णाजिनान्तं च मा मैन्द्र्यं ज्यैष्ठ्यम्̐ श्रैष्ठ्यं व्यौषीर् इति पुत्रायैनत् प्रदाय वरुणप्रघासवत् स्नानप्रभृय् आ समिदाधानात् ॥
10.9.m: And handing over to his son the border of the black-antelope skin with: 'May you not take away my Indra-like power, seniority, and pre-eminence', [the procedure takes place] as in the Varuṇapraghāsa, from the bathing up to the placing of the kindling stick.

10.9.s: ud vayam ity unnetronnītā āmahīyāṃ japanto gachanti \\ apāma somam amṛtā abhūma \\ aganma jyotir avidāma devān \ kiṃ nūnam asmān kṛṇavad arātiḥ \ kim u dhūrtir amṛta martyasya \\ iti //
10.9.d: उद् वयम् इत्य् उन्नेत्रोन्नीता आमहीयां जपन्तो गछन्ति \\ अपाम सोमम् अमृता अभूम \\ अगन्म ज्योतिर् अविदाम देवान् \ किं नूनम् अस्मान् कृणवद् अरातिः \ किम् उ धूर्तिर् अमृत मर्त्यस्य \\ इति ॥
10.9.m: Brought forth by the Unnetṛ priest with: 'Upwards we [have risen]…', they proceed muttering the Āmahīyā [verse]: 'We have drunk the soma, we have become immortal; / we have reached the light, we have found the gods. / What can malice do to us now? / What can the deceit of a mortal do, O immortal?'
The sacrificer sits behind the Śālādvārya fire, placing the black-antelope skin on his lap.

10.9.s: sruvāhutiṃ juhoti maindryaṃ jyaiṣṭhyam̐ śraiṣṭhyam agnir dadhātu svāhā \\ iti //
10.9.d: स्रुवाहुतिं जुहोति मैन्द्र्यं ज्यैष्ठ्यम्̐ श्रैष्ठ्यम् अग्निर् दधातु स्वाहा \\ इति ॥
10.9.m: He offers a ladleful offering with: 'May Agni bestow Indra-like power, seniority, and pre-eminence upon me, svāhā.'
Having laid down the black-antelope skin, the Udayanīyā rite is [performed] like the Prāyaṇīyā.
Pathyā Svasti is the fourth [deity].

10.9.s: pātraprokṣaṇādy ājyāsādanāt savanīyavat parivyayaṇādi maitrāvaruṇī vaśānūbandhyā //
10.9.d: पात्रप्रोक्षणाद्य् आज्यासादनात् सवनीयवत् परिव्ययणादि मैत्रावरुणी वशानूबन्ध्या ॥
10.9.m: From the sprinkling of the vessels up to the placing of the clarified butter, it is like the Savanīyā [animal sacrifice]; beginning with the encircling, the Anūbandhyā is a sterile cow for Mitra and Varuṇa.
Or [it begins] with the hiding of the Svaru-chip, because [the preceding actions] have already been performed.
Some say: having placed it, [the rite proceeds] from the clarified butter portions up to the Iḍā.
The Udavasānīyā is [a cake] on five potsherds for Agni, [offered] on the fire churned out of the mounted [fires].
[It is] a subsidiary of the soma sacrifice, because of proximity and absence of conflict.
Or it is an obligatory [daily rite], because of the scriptural rule about the morning oblation;

10.9.d: अत्यग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यः षोडशी वाजपेयो ऽतिरात्रो ऽप्तोर्यामः ॥
10.9.m: the Atyagniṣṭoma, Ukthya, Ṣoḍaśin, Vājapeya, Atirātra, and Aptoryāma.

10.9.s: teṣām ukthyo 'chāvākam abhi saṃtiṣṭhate hotāram itare //
10.9.d: तेषाम् उक्थ्यो ऽछावाकम् अभि संतिष्ठते होतारम् इतरे ॥
10.9.m: Of these, the Ukthya concludes after the Acchāvāka priest; the others, after the Hotṛ priest.

10.9.s: vaiśyarājanyayoḥ some nyagrodhastibhīn upanahyechan bhakṣāya krayaṇaprabhṛty anusomam āvṛtā samānam āsādanaṃ prāg abhiṣavāt //
10.9.d: वैश्यराजन्ययोः सोमे न्यग्रोधस्तिभीन् उपनह्येछन् भक्षाय क्रयणप्रभृत्य् अनुसोमम् आवृता समानम् आसादनं प्राग् अभिषवात् ॥
10.9.m: In the soma sacrifice of a Vaiśya or Rājanya, if he desires to tie up shoots of the Nyagrodha tree for consumption, [the procedure is] identical according to the soma ritual from the buying [of soma] onwards; their placing takes place before the pressing.
Or having brought [the shoots] at the time of drawing into the cups and crushing them with curd, he draws [it] into that cup following [the rest].

10.9.s: hūyamāneṣu kuśataruṇena juhoti \\ ahaṃ tvad asmi \\ iti //
10.9.d: हूयमानेषु कुशतरुणेन जुहोति \\ अहं त्वद् अस्मि \\ इति ॥
10.9.m: While [the oblations] are being offered, he offers with a fresh shoot of Kuśa grass: 'I am from you.'

11.1.m: He remains restrained in speech while the ritual action is taking place.

11.1.d: हिरण्यवत्याम्̐ हुतायां दक्षिणो ऽनुगछत्य् आ क्रयात् ॥
11.1.m: When the [oblation] accompanied by gold has been offered, he follows along on the south side up to the purchase [of soma].

11.1.s: krīte prāṅ atītya pūrveṇānaḥ parītyāpareṇa vā dakṣiṇo 'nugachaty ā nidhānāt //
11.1.d: क्रीते प्राङ् अतीत्य पूर्वेणानः परीत्यापरेण वा दक्षिणो ऽनुगछत्य् आ निधानात् ॥
11.1.m: When [the soma] is purchased, having gone across to the east, having walked around the cart by the east or by the west, he follows along on the south side up to the deposit.
Or behind the Dakṣiṇāgni during the Gharma offering.
When [the Adhvaryu] is about to carry the Stambayajus, he sits to the south of the Āhavanīya place together with the vedi.
Thus everywhere prior to the bringing forward of Agni and Soma.
Or following each successive rite together [with it],

11.1.d: आहवनीये प्रणीयमाने ऽप्रतिरथस्य द्वादश ब्रुवन्न् अग्नौ ॥
11.1.m: while the Āhavanīya fire is being led forward, he recites the twelve [verses] of the Apratiratha hymn over the fire.
When [the vedi] is strewn, he goes as required.
For the bringing forward of Agni and Soma, having gone north of the Dhiṣṇya hearths and east of the Śālādvārya fire, he sits on the south.
And when the oblation is offered, taking the soma, he follows the fire.
Or the sacrificer may carry the soma.
Having handed it to another, while it is not yet deposited, having gone as he came, he sits to the south.
And when the oblation is offered, taking the soma and going past the Āhavanīya fire,
in the latter part of the night, if he wishes, [he acts] as during the bringing forward of Agni and Soma.

11.1.s: vipruṣām̐ homam̐ hutvā pratihartāram anvārabheta vādīkṣitaḥ //
11.1.d: विप्रुषाम्̐ होमम्̐ हुत्वा प्रतिहर्तारम् अन्वारभेत वादीक्षितः ॥
11.1.m: Having offered the oblation of drops, the consecrated sacrificer may take hold of the Pratihartṛ priest from behind.

11.1.s: prastotrāmantritas \\ etaṃ te deva savitaḥ \ stuta savituḥ prasave \\ ity uktvā prasauti //
11.1.d: प्रस्तोत्रामन्त्रितस् \\ एतं ते देव सवितः \ स्तुत सवितुः प्रसवे \\ इत्य् उक्त्वा प्रसौति ॥
11.1.m: Invited by the Prastotṛ, having uttered, "This for you, god Savitṛ; chant at the instigation of Savitṛ," he gives permission.

11.1.s: deva savitar etad bṛhaspate pra \\ iti vā //
11.1.d: देव सवितर् एतद् बृहस्पते प्र \\ इति वा ॥
11.1.m: Or with: "God Savitṛ, this; Bṛhaspati, chant!"
Or with: "By the ray for truth," according to each mantra.
Gliding [takes place] by that [way] through which the entrance [was made].
If [he enters] after going around the sacrificial post by the east, [he glides] by the west.
He sits to the south of the Praśāstṛ.
The others [sit] to the west of the dhiṣṇya hearths.
During the pavamāna chant, the movement after completion [is] to the north of the Praśāstṛ's dhiṣṇya hearth.

12.1.m: The rules of the Jyotiṣṭoma [apply] to the one-day sacrifice and to the twelve-day sacrifice, because its qualities are seen [in them].
Because of the statement [that they apply] to the Vrātyastomas and Sādyaḥkras [derived] from the first [i.e., the one-day sacrifice].
The twelve-day sacrifice is [both] a sacrificial session and a multi-day sacrifice.

12.1.s: āsata upayantīti sattraliṅgaṃ yajata ity ahīnasya //
12.1.d: आसत उपयन्तीति सत्त्रलिङ्गं यजत इत्य् अहीनस्य ॥
12.1.m: "They sit," "they undertake" are the distinctive marks of a sacrificial session; "he sacrifices" [is the mark] of a multi-day sacrifice.
A sacrificial session has Atirātras at both ends; of a multi-day sacrifice, [the Atirātra is] at the end.
All are sacrificers in sacrificial sessions.
And [they are] without sacrificial gifts, because of the conjunction of the masters.
The householder performs the duties of the sacrificer, because of [the others] not being enjoined.
When it is impossible, there is touching of the householder.
In rites for the sake of another, one [acts], because it is already accomplished.

12.1.s: agniṃ ceṣyamāṇāḥ samārohya gṛhapatir madhye manthaty ardhaśa itare dakṣiṇottarāḥ //
12.1.d: अग्निं चेष्यमाणाः समारोह्य गृहपतिर् मध्ये मन्थत्य् अर्धश इतरे दक्षिणोत्तराः ॥
12.1.m: Intending to pile the fire, having mounted [the fires], the householder churns in the middle; the others [churn] divided into halves, south and north.
The throwing of embers [takes place] into the householder's Āhavanīya fire.
There [an animal victim] sacred to Prajāpati [is offered].
The Patnīsaṃyāja offerings are made with ghee, except for the householder's [wife].
In case of inability, the fixed rite [is performed] everywhere on the fires that are mounted and churned out.
At the time of consecration, churning [is performed] in the north-beamed hall as before.
The throwing [of embers takes place] into the Gārhapatya fire here.

12.1.s: upavasathaprabhṛti prāg anīṣomapraṇayanād upaśamayya cinoty enāñ chālādvaryād dakṣiṇottarān dhiṣṇyavad vā śruteḥ //
12.1.d: उपवसथप्रभृति प्राग् अनीषोमप्रणयनाद् उपशमय्य चिनोत्य् एनाञ् छालाद्वर्याद् दक्षिणोत्तरान् धिष्ण्यवद् वा श्रुतेः ॥
12.1.m: Beginning from the Upavasatha day, prior to the carrying forward of the Agnīṣoma, having extinguished them, he piles them south to north from the Śālādvārya fire, or like the dhiṣṇya hearths, because of scripture.
Or, as prescribed, for the householder.
